title: IEBC scoops the Best Independent Commission Stand Award at the 2025 Nairobi International Trade Fair20th Oct 2025
text: The Commission participated in this year’s Nairobi International Trade Fair that was open from 29th September to 5th October 2025 at the Jamhuri Park Showground. This is one of the opportunistic events that the Commission uses to showcase its services to the public. This year, among the services that were offered at the IEBC stand included registration of voters and voter education. Many visitor walked in the IEBC exhibition stand and got the opportunity to learn more about elections and their participation in the election process. The stand won the Best Independent Commission Stand Award with Nairobi County Elections Manager (CEM) Albert Gogo at hand to receive the award on behalf of the Commission Chairoerson from H.E President William Samoei Ruto. “Hongera IEBC Join us in celebrating the Best Independent Commission Stand Award at the 2025 Nairobi International Trade Fair!” Besides learning about elections and their participation, the visitors took the chance to register as new voters or transfer their particulars to polling stations of their choice and also confirmed their status of registration.

title: IEBC develops Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, pledges to observe prudent financial planning and accountability20th Oct 2025
text: The Commission led by Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC, convened at the serane Sawela Lodges in Naivasha from 22nd to 26th September 2025 to develop its Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) for the financial years 2026/27, 2027/28, and 2028/29. The Chaiperson observed that at the heart of the budget preparation process is a commitment to prudent financial planning, expenditure and accountability guaranteeing value for money while enhancing service delivery. While opening the workshop, Ethekon noted: “History reminds us that credible elections are not born on Election Day. They are built here in strategic meetings like this, where planning meets responsibility.” The Chairperson underscored the need for integrity in budgeting and to help the country manage election costs by optimizing scarce resources without compromising quality. “When we work on these numbers, they must not be arbitrary. Every proposal must be realistic, rational and aligned with our institutional goals. The budget we shape here is not just about figures it is the blueprint for building trust, credibility and confidence in our electoral process,” said Ethekon. The Commission’s Vice-Chairperson, Ms. Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW, who chairs the Finance & Procurement Committee, emphasized that the workshop marks the foundation of financial planning and electoral readiness for the next three years. She emphasized on the need to create a budget that complies with National Treasury circular, supports IEBC operations, reflects economic realities, and upholds the Commission’s constitutional mandate. The 10th August 2027 General Election falls within the current MTEF and the Commission has begun engaging the National Treasury as well as committees of parliament to ensure timely planning, allocation and disbursement of funds for the preparation and management of elections.

title: IEBC meets Political Parties Liaison Committee to enhance collaboration, provides update on conduct of by-elections19th Oct 2025
text: The Commission led by Chairman Erastus Ethekon and supported by Elgia Afric held an introductory meeting with the Political Parties Liaison Committee (PPLC). The PPLC serves as a platform for dialogue and collaboration between the Commission and the Office of the Registrar of Political Parties, in accordance with paragraph 9(2) of the Second Schedule of the IEBC Act, Cap 7C, and section 38 of the Political Parties Act, Cap 7D. The Commission’s engagement with the PPLC aimed to enhance collaboration by introducing the Commission to political parties, providing an update on preparations for the upcoming by-elections, sharing plans and timelines for the commencement of Continuous Voter Registration and discussing structured modalities for future interactions between the Commission and political parties.. “We come together not as separate entities but as partners united by a common responsibility to protect the will of the Kenyan people through credible, peaceful and inclusive elections,” said Ethekon. Ethekon observed that since the Commission came onboard, it had been on a significant learning journey by engaging stakeholders. “We began by meeting the Steering Committee of the PPLC, recognizing that every political party, regardless of size, plays a crucial role in fostering public trust in the electoral process. Hence, today’s plenary meeting is of great importance,” he noted. Commissioner MaryKaren Sorobit, Chairperson of the Legal Compliance and Political Liaison Committee, welcomed representatives from all political parties to the meeting. “Your presence emphasizes the importance of partnership in safeguarding the credibility and integrity of our elections,” she remarked. Commissioner Marykaren emphasized that the meeting aims to establish a framework for a sustained partnership. Evans Misati, the Chairperson of the PPLC, highlighted the invaluable role of the committee in promoting dialogue, building consensus and promoting political tolerance. This is particularly crucial as the country gears up for the upcoming by-elections and the launch of Continuous Voter Registration on Monday, alongside other significant functions of the Commission that will take place in the near future. Ms. Sophia Sitati, Ag. Registrar of Political Parties, called upon the three institutions to collaborate continuously to ensure that democracy is strengthened through coordinated efforts, transparent processes and inclusive participation. “As we look to the future, the voices of political parties are vital in shaping the quality and credibility of our elections. May you act as ambassadors of the Commission, promoting transparency, integrity and peaceful democratic participation within your parties and the broader public,” said Sitati. Marjan underscored that IEBC values the PPLC not merely as a statutory body or a formality but as an essential forum for strengthening Kenya’s democracy and good electoral governance.

title: Commission resumes Continuous Voter Registration with colourful launch at Mashuuru Primary School in Kajiado19th Oct 2025
text: It was a great honour to stand before you as we launched the commencement of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR). This exercise is not simply an administrative duty—it is the heartbeat of our democracy. It is here that citizens transform from bystanders into active nation-builders. The Constitution of Kenya, under Article 88, mandates the Commission to conduct continuous voter registration and to regularly revise the voters’ register. A credible register of voters is the foundation of a free, fair, and inclusive electoral process. IEBC Chairperson Erustus Edung Ethekon, HSC,noted that this CVR exercise will take place in all 290 constituencies, supported by 57 Huduma Centres for accessibility. Transfers and corrections will continue to be handled in constituency offices. The Commission projects a register of 28.5 million voters in 2027. To reach this, we have designed a phased approach: CVR (10%) – commencing 29th September, 2025; First Enhanced CVR (40%) – after conclusion of the 27th November, 2025 by-elections; Second Enhanced CVR (50%) – beginning in the next financial year. Ethekon said the Commission has upgraded its technology by integrating a new Biometric Voter Registration module into the KIEMS system, allowing for faster, more secure, and more reliable services.. For this phase, 24,128 registration centres have been gazetted, ensuring equity and security across the country. “I appeal to the youth, who make up more than 75% of our population, if you are not yet registered, this is your chance. Registering today is your voice in tomorrow’s election. By building a credible register, we are safeguarding the integrity of the 2027 General Election. Let us all take responsibility and ensure every eligible Kenyan is counted,” said Ethekon. “This voter registration exercise is the heartbeat of our democracy. It transforms citizens into active nation builders. Credible voter registration is the foundation of any free and fair election. Without it, the integrity of the process cannot be guaranteed.” The Commission observed that this exercise gives the citizens the opportunity to transfer their vote to preferred area. “I urge the people of Kajiado, and all Kenyans, to take advantage of this chance,” said Ethekon. “Today marks the beginning of nationwide voter registration. After the November by-election, we will launch a mass registration drive across the country. We have upgraded our technology to make tallying faster, more secure, and more reliable, ensuring that every vote counts.” “Registration centres have been aligned and made more accessible to ensure inclusivity. In addition, mobile registration units will reach those in remote areas.” The Chairperson reiterated that the youth make up 70% of likely voters and urged them to register today and make their voices heard tomorrow. “The future of our nation depends on your participation,” said Ethekon. Commissioner Ann Nderitu, CBS the Chairperson of the Electoral Operations Committee said Voter registration is the foundation of democracy and that when people register, they claim their rightful place in shaping the future of Kenya. “This register is the backbone of electoral preparedness and the guarantee of credible elections. Without it, our democracy cannot stand, she said. “With gazetted registration officers, the mapping and realignment of registration centres, and the deployment of new voter registration technology, IEBC has demonstrated its commitment to credible elections.” Commissioner Nderitu noted that the Commission has put in place measures to ensure the 2027 General Election is fair, accurate, and balanced. This commitment must be matched by citizens stepping forward to register. “Collaboration is key to the success of this voter registration exercise. County governments, civil society, and citizens must all play their part,” she added.

title: Commission call staff to action, to serve with sacrifice and patriotism as Continuous Voter Registration resumes29th Sep 2025
text: The Commission convened all its staff, from across the country, for a landmark training on Continuous Voter Registration (CVR), a mission that carries the weight of Kenya’s democratic destiny. Led by IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, the Commission reminded its staff that they are more than officers behind a desk—they are the living face of Kenya’s democracy, from the remotest polling station in Turkana to the headquarters in Nairobi. “You are the face of the Commission,” declared Ethekon with patriotic fervor. “How you serve, communicate and carry yourselves defines what Kenyans think of the IEBC.” The Chairperson saluted the Commission’s staff for their sacrifice, endurance and courage in delivering elections that the world recognized as credible and peaceful. “Many of you have worked long hours, in difficult conditions, sometimes hostile environments, yet you never wavered. Because of you, the Commission delivered for Kenya—and for democracy,” said Ethekon. With the 2027 General Election in sight, the Chairperson urged staff to rise to the challenge. “Communicate better, serve better, and work better—together. Speak clearly, engage openly, and share accurate information. Remember, every citizen matters. Treat Kenyans with dignity and professionalism.” The Commission projects to enroll an additional 6.3 million new voters, raising Kenya’s electoral voice to over 28 million strong. Commissioner Ann Nderitu, CBS, underscored that CVR is not a box-ticking exercise but the foundation of credible elections. “Without an accurate, inclusive and trusted register, everything else we do falls short,” she said. “These are not just statistics. They are voices shaping Kenya’s future. Each registration is more than data—it is an act of empowerment, a restoration of dignity, a reaffirmation of the constitutional right to choose one’s leaders.” Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan Hussein Marjan, MBS reminded the staff that their role transcends technical procedures. “Training is not just about skills. It is about inspiring trust and confidence in every Kenyan. You are not just doing a job—you are protecting the integrity of Kenya’s democracy,” said Marjan. As the sun set over Naivasha, the message was clear: every registration is a shield for democracy, every interaction a step towards national unity, and every staff member a custodian of Kenya’s destiny. The journey to 2027 has begun, and with it, the call to service, sacrifice, and patriotism.

title: Commission targets 6.3 million new voters on resumption of Continuous Voter Registration exercise29th Sep 2025
text: The Commission Chairperson, Erastus Edung Ethekon, has assured the public that IEBC is fully prepared and working diligently for the forthcoming by-elections as a precursor to the 2027 General Election. He emphasized that preparations for the by-elections are on course. On resumption of Continuous Voter Registration, the Chairperson stated that the Commission aims to enlist 6.3 million new eligible voters, 70 percent of whom are youth. This assurance came during his appearance before the Parliamentary Accounts Committee, led by Butere Member of the National Assembly Hon. Tindi Mwale, where the Commission had been invited to respond to the Auditor General’s report on Account of the National Government for the Financial year ended 30th June 2023. The Chairperson also pledged to maintain close collaboration with the leadership of both houses of Parliament and the various committees, as well as other stakeholders. “We have an open-door policy and remain committed to working closely with the leadership of both houses of Parliament and all progressive Kenyans to enhance our electoral processes and voter experience,” said Ethekon.

title: Commission meets Returning Officers, discusses operations and logistics requirements to conduct by-elections29th Sep 2025
text: The IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC and Members of the Commission on 18th September, 2025 met gazetted Returning Officers and staff involved in planning and conducting the 24 by-elections across the country. The planning meeting discussed the operations and logistics requirements to conduct by-elections including 1 Senatorial, 6 Member of National Assembly, and 17 Member of County Assembly on 27th November 2025. “As Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) plans for these by-elections, know that the expectations are high and scrutiny will be intense and you should rise to the occasion. The country is anxious and keen to evaluate the kind of Commission in place under my leadership. I believe in this Secretariat staff and will work with them to deliver the sovereign will of Kenyans. As Chairperson I’m not only here to provide leadership, but to be led by you to conduct these by-elections. I expect collegiality, mutual respect and collective responsibility from all of us,” said Ethekon. The Chairperson urged Returning Officers to remain focused and adhere to the rule of law. “Time and again you have displayed high mastery of your job. I have no doubt in your professionalism and credibility to deliver on this exercise. This team led by Returning Officers in each of the 24 by-election has been vetted and found to be trustworthy and can go beyond the normal call of duty to deliver the results. “Let Kenyans feel the values of integrity, impartiality and transparency when we deliver these by-elections, which are competitive. Show your integrity, be professional, do the right thing and stand up for what is right,” said Ethekon. The Chairperson observed that Kenyans are demanding IEBC to improve on the duration of time in results transmission, enhance information sharing and communication. He urged staff to engage all stakeholders, inform and educate them on Commission processes and timelines. Commissioner Marykaren Sorobit urged the Returning Officers and their teams to do proper planning and assured them of the Commission’s support. “We have faith in our staff because you have the experience. You can only perfect it. Planning is everything, if we get it right we will deliver the results,” said Sorobit. Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan Hussein Marjan, MBS noted that the by-elections matter deeply to Kenyans and scrutiny of the processes will be intense. “For voters it is a democratic right, for the Commission it provides a platform to prove its crediblility and dependability. Priorities are clear including logistic readiness, staff training, effective stakeholder engagements, security coordination and accurate results management. Each of you carry a responsibility that will define the credibility of the Commission. This is an opportunity to show we are not only ready for the 24 by-election in November but also the 2027 General Election,” said Marjan.

title: Commission administers Oath of Secrecy to gazetted Returning Officers ahead of by-elections29th Sep 2025
text: The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) ’s legal team led by Direcor of Legal Services (DLS) Chrispine Owiye, OGW on Friday, 19th September, 2025 oversaw the administration of Oath of Secrecy of the Ballot to gazetted Returning Officers and other IEBC staff at the end of a joint National Planning meeting in Naivasha. The Officers will be involved in the conduct of the 24 By-Elections across the country on 27th November 2025. The 24 By-Elections are for Member of Senate - Baringo County (1); Members of the National Assembly for Banissa, Kasipul, Magarini, Malava, Mbeere North and Ugunja Constituencies (6); Members of County Assemblies: Angata Nanyokie Ward in Samburu County, Chemundu/Kapng’etuny Ward in Nandi County, Chewani Ward in Tana River County, Fafi Ward in Garissa County and Kariobangi North Ward in Nairobi City County. Others are Kisa East Ward in Kakamega County, Metkei Ward in Elgeyo Marakwet County, Mumbuni North Ward in Machakos County, Narok Town Ward in Narok County, Purko Ward in Kajiado County, Tembelio Ward in Uasin Gishu County, Nyansiongo, Nyamaiya, Ekerenyo Wards in Nyamira County, Kabuchai/Chwele Ward in Bungoma County, Lake Zone and Nanaam Wards in Turkana County (17). The campaign period runs from 8th October 2025 and ceases on 24th November 2025, being 48 hours before the by-election day between 7:00 am and 6:00 pm. Political parties and candidates are to appoint and submit the names of their agents 14 days before the date of the by-elections to facilitate the processing of their details and training.

title: Commission engages Diaspora Affairs to enhance participation of citizens residing outside Kenya in elections29th Sep 2025
text: The Commission, led by Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW, held a consultative meeting last week with Roseline Njogu, CBS, Principal Secretary, State Department for Diaspora Affairs (SSDA) on modalities to enhance Kenya’s participation in the Diaspora Election processes. Ms. Fahima, representing the Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, acknowledged that Kenyans in diaspora are a valuable national asset, who must be involved in the nation’s democratic and governance process. “They contribute socially, economically and politically to the country. With over one million Kenyans living abroad, diaspora remittances now standing at Ksh 6.5 billions, rank among the top sources of foreign exchange. Therefore, engaging them in national processes, including elections, is both strategic and essential,” said the Vice Chairperson. The Constitution of Kenya and Elections Act of 2011 provide for the progressive realization of voting rights for citizens residing outside Kenya. Since 2013, The Commission has facilitated diaspora participation in Presidential elections in accordance with these legal provisions. The Vice Chairperson further highlighted that in 2022, the Commission facilitated voting in 12 countries including Burundi, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, South Sudan, South Africa, the USA, Canada, the United Kingdom, Germany, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Qatar. In the run up to the 2022 General Election, the Commission had a total of 10,443 registered voters in Diaspora. “The Commission faces significant challenges despite these achievements in implementing the Diaspora Election process, including low voter registration numbers, operational and logistical limitations, legal and policy constraints, limited awareness and voter education, and the perception of tokenism,” said Ms Fahima. The Principal Secretary stated that the State Department for Diaspora Affairs is committed to enhancing the participation of Kenyans abroad in the democratic process. Commissioner Dr. Alutalala Mukhwana, the Chairperson of the Voter Education, Partnerships, Stakeholder Engagement and Communications Committee, stressed that citizens living outside Kenya have every right to participate in elections. “The Commission is committed to finding ways to facilitate this participation and is seeking a collaborative partnership with SDDA to identify existing gaps and develop data-driven strategies that will ensure the diaspora’s participation in elections,” said Dr Alutalala. Marjan Hussein Marjan, MBS, the Commission Secretary/CEO, added that the Commission will continue to enhance diaspora participation guided by the 2025 population estimates that puts 1.46 million Kenyans living abroad, with 629,688 registered with Kenya High Commissions, Embassies and consulates. “The Commission remains committed to expanding and strengthening diaspora participation guided by updated data and strategic partnerships. With reforms, expanded access and sustained collaboration, diaspora participation will continue to grow and strengthen Kenya’s democracy,” said Marjan.

title: IEBC identifies, tutors Training of Trainers ahead of national launch of Continuous Voter Registration exercise19th Sep 2025
text: The Commission Secretary/CEO Hussein Marjan Hussein, MBS, on 9th September, 2025 opened the National Training of Trainers (ToTs) workshop for the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR). Training program, was tailor made in preparation for the resumption of the CVR exercise, which will launched in Kajiado County on 29th September, 2025. “As we formally begin the Training of Trainers for the upcoming Continuous Voter Registration exercise, this workshop marks a pivotal step in the Commission’s journey toward delivering a credible and inclusive 2027 General Election,” he said. According to Article 88(4)(b) of the Constitution of Kenya, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission is mandated to conduct continuous voter registration and regularly revise the voter register. This is not a discretionary task; it is a constitutional and legal duty that we must execute with both urgency and excellence. This training was not merely a scheduled event but it represented a strategic investment in the credibility of Kenya’s democracy. He urged participants to uphold integrity. “Integrity is not a suggestion, it is a condition of service,” said Marjan. The CEO emphasized that every decision and action must reflect the highest standards of honesty, impartiality and professionalism, as public trust in this institution is earned and is a collective responsibility. The training workshop addressed all aspects of the CVR process, from operational procedures to the technical details of the new Kenya Integrated Election Management System’s (KIEMS) voter registration module. The approach targeted to ensure consistency and standardization of electoral operations across all levels and offices of the Commission. Additionally, it will facilitate a uniform application of electoral laws, procedures, and technologies while enhancing preparedness and risk management for the CVR exercise. This training program is designed for both field Registration Officers and headquarters staff. The Master Trainers, responsible for developing the training content, will act as the lead trainers for the (ToTs) program. Afterwards, the ToTs will train registration officers in the to prepare for the resumption of the CVR exercise. The objective is to ensure that all levels of the Commission are fully equipped and ready for the start of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) process.

title: Commission trains Political Parties on use of Candidate Registration Management System ahead of by-election exercise19th Sep 2025
text: The Commission on 8th September, 2025 conducted a technical training on the Candidate Registration Management System (CRMS) for Political Parties’ IT administrators. The objective of the training was to equip IT administrators with the skills required to accurately and efficiently upload their parties’ candidates’ details into the system in preparation for the 27th November 2025 By-Elections. Chrisphine Owiye, OGW, Director of Legal Services, welcomed participants to what he termed a significant exercise in the by-election calendar. He explained that the training was designed to impart practical skills on uploading candidate details into CRMS, linking the process to constitutional obligations under Article 88(4). “This exercise is anchored in the Constitution, which mandates the Commission to regulate political party nominations and register candidates for election. Your role is not just administrative but central to safeguarding the integrity of democratic elections,” he said. Moses Sunkuli, OGW, Director of Electoral Operations, echoed the importance of the training, describing it as a milestone in the Commission’s preparedness for the by-elections. He reassured participants that their requirements had been catered for and encouraged them to make the most of the session. “You are our key stakeholders, and we remain fully available to address any questions or concerns you may have. Let us all remain attentive and ensure this training equips you with the necessary skills,” he noted. Ruth Kulundu, DCS–Operations, urged political parties to exercise diligence and responsibility, stressing that the quality of leadership presented to the public directly influences trust in institutions. She emphasized that accurate uploading of candidate details would help Returning Officers expedite the registration process. Obadiah Keitany, OGW, DCS Support Services, described the CRMS training as an important milestone in the electoral calendar, bringing together the Commission and its key stakeholders. He highlighted the system’s role in ensuring transparency and accountability. “The system reduces bureaucracy, secures data storage, and even features a tracking mechanism, meaning all actions in the system are logged and traceable in case of mischief,” he explained. Commissioner Marykaren Sorobit welcomed participants, noting that the CRMS program, introduced in 2013, has undergone continuous improvement to enhance its reliability and strengthen election integrity. She emphasized that the adoption of technology, including CRMS, is central to transparency and efficiency. “This training will help us deliver free, fair, and credible elections, which all of us can account for. As a Commission, we remain fully available to provide guidance and consultation throughout the process,” she affirmed. Commissioner Ann Nderitu, CBS, officially opened the training workshop, describing it as a critical step in preparations for the by-elections. She commended political parties for adhering to Commission timelines and underscored the importance of attention to detail when entering candidate information. Tracing the CRMS journey since its 2013 launch, she outlined its achievements in digitizing nominations, generating statutory forms and reports, supporting ballot preparation, and improving data accuracy and security. “This time, it is you who is plotting the data for your candidate. Any error must be attributed to the political party. That’s why your understanding of the system is critical,” she emphasized. She called for accuracy, efficiency, and integrity, highlighting inclusion and stakeholder participation as guiding principles of CRMS. Concluding her remarks, Commissioner Nderitu wished participants fruitful deliberations and officially declared the training workshop open.

title: IEBC partners with Media Council of Kenya to enhance access to accurate electoral information and promote transparency19th Sep 2025
text: The Commission and the Media Council of Kenya (MCK) have entered into a strategic partnership through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at strengthening the role of the media in the electoral process. Speaking during the signing of the Memorandum of Understanding today, IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC, welcomed the collaboration with the MCK, describing it as a significant milestone in strengthening cooperation between the two institutions. He explained that the MoU serves as a quasi-legal framework outlining areas of partnership such as training journalists on electoral processes, building the capacity of Commission staff on media relations, accrediting journalists for election coverage, and monitoring media content to curb hate speech, ethnic incitement, harassment, and other risks that could undermine peaceful elections. The partnership will also establish information hubs to enhance access to accurate electoral information, empower voters, and promote transparency. “This MoU allows us to set up robust mechanisms for training, accreditation, and media monitoring, while also educating citizens especially digital content creators on how the information they share impacts democracy and the integrity of our elections,” said Chairperson Ethekon. David Omwoyo Omwoyo, MBS, the CEO of the MCK, hailed the signing of the Memorandum of Understanding with the IEBC as a timely and important step in strengthening public trust in the electoral process. He emphasized the critical role of clear and credible media coverage in sustaining confidence in the Commission, noting that every Kenyan relies on the IEBC to conduct credible elections that safeguard peace and national stability. Mr. Omwoyo outlined the areas of engagement under the MoU, which include fact-checking through tools such as iVerify, training of journalists, revising the guidelines on election coverage, developing a training manual, and establishing media hubs across the country to equip media practitioners with knowledge on electoral matters. He also stressed the importance of tackling the growing challenge of technology-driven disinformation and AI-generated fake news, calling for greater investment in tech-savvy approaches to safeguard information integrity. “It is critical to ensure that the credibility of IEBC is sustained by fostering clear, accurate and professional media coverage, because the trust of Kenyans in the electoral process is the foundation for peace and the welfare of our nation,” said Mr. Omwoyo. He further commended Commissioner @AlutalalaDr for his proactive engagement with the media, which, he noted, reinforces confidence in IEBC as a credible election management body. Commissioner Dr. Alutalala Mukhwana, the Chairperson of the Voter Education, Partnerships, Communications and Stakeholder Engagement Committee expressed gratitude to the Chairperson for the opportunity to address the media on electoral matters, noting that effective communication is vital in ensuring that the Commission’s work is visible and positively represented. He emphasized that in Kenya’s political environment, the success of the Commission is closely tied to how elections are managed and communicated to the public. He thanked the MCK for its support, urging it to move swiftly in providing the necessary assistance outlined in the MoU. He highlighted the importance of cooperation between the two institutions in safeguarding national stability and building public trust in the electoral process. “The Chairperson has always insisted on an open-door policy, and I want to assure you that we are ready to engage and consult at any time, because everything we do is for the nation,” said Commissioner Dr. Alutalala. He concluded by acknowledging the Department of Voter Education, Partnerships, and Communications for its central role in making the partnership possible.

title: IEBC pays courtesy call on Prime Cabinet Secretary, discusses progress and priorities in preparation for 2027 GE19th Sep 2025
text: IEBC, led by Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, HSC, paid a courtesy call on the Prime Cabinet Secretary and Cabinet Secretary for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs, H.E. Dr. Hon Musalia W Mudavadi, EGH, at his office. IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, HSC conveyed warm regards to the Office of the Prime Cabinet Secretary and Cabinet Secretary for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs, while highlighting the Commission’s progress and priorities as it prepares for the 2027 General Election. He noted that since assuming office, the Commission has undergone a comprehensive induction process that equipped its members with the skills required to deliver credible elections. To enhance efficiency, roles have been distributed among commissioners, each heading a committee aligned to the institution’s mandate. The Chairperson further underscored the Commission’s commitment to stakeholder engagement, citing recent consultations with the heads of missions at the British High Commission, the Media Council of Kenya, civil society organizations, security stakeholders in Mombasa, the Judicial Service Commission and the Head of Public Service. Others were the Cabinet Secretary to the Treasury, the Political Parties Liaison Committee, the National Cohesion and Integration Commission, the British High Commissioner, the UNDP Resident Representative, and other governance partners. These engagements, he explained, have been critical in fostering inclusivity and building synergies for free, fair, credible, and peaceful elections. He also emphasized the importance of collaboration with the Ministry of Foreign and Diaspora Affairs in engaging diaspora voters through voter registration and civic education. Additionally, he appealed for whole-ofgovernment support, particularly in the timely and adequate resourcing of the Commission. This, he noted, would ensure smooth operations, robust civic education, enhanced security measures, and strengthened inter-agency coordination. The Chairperson disclosed that the Commission has sought concurrence from the Prime Cabinet Secretary and the Cabinet Secretary for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs to allow the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) to extend support to the Commission. This will be preceded by a Needs Assessment Mission aimed at identifying priority areas where the UN and development partners can provide coordinated and timely electoral assistance, in line with the electoral cycle approach. “As a Commission, we are determined to deliver credible elections, but this requires adequate resourcing, strong partnerships, and timely support across government and with our development partners,” said Chairperson. Mudavadi congratulated the commissioners for their appointment and told them that serving Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) was a privilege. He asked the commissioners to serve with humility, resilience and forthrightness. “Do not compromise on your independence as an EMB. Ensure you live up to the expectations of the Kenyan people by conducting free, fair, and credible elections,” said Mudavadi. He assured the Commission of his office’s support and facilitation in meeting its requirements, particularly in matters relating to engagement with the diaspora community. In particular, the PCS assured IEBC of his support in accessing, enhancing and optimizing diaspora participation in electoral process; and in liasing with the relevant state and non state actors, including international community, in raising requisite resource support.

title: Commissioner Dr. Alutalala engages media, highlights IEBC Roadmap to 2027 General Election14th Sep 2025
text: The Chairperson of the Voter Education, Partnerships, Communications and Stakeholder Engagement Committee, Commissioner Dr. Mukhwana Alutalala, recently appeared on several media platforms including Nation FM, Spice FM, and TV 47 to update the public on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission’s (IEBC) preparations for the upcoming key electoral activities leading to the 2027 elections. Dr. Alutalala elaborated on the establishment of Commission Committees designed to enhance efficient coordination across various Directorates and thematic areas, supporting the effective implementation of the Commission’s Constitutional mandate. Addressing concerns over public trust and confidence in the electoral process, Commissioner Alutalala emphasized IEBC’s commitment to transparency through timely communication and continuous engagement with stakeholders. He highlighted the strategic focus on reaching young voters, who constitute over 70% of Kenya’s population, with tailored voter education and communication campaigns aimed at first-time and new voters. Dr. Alutalala acknowledged Kenya’s complex electoral history and the high stakes associated with the elections as key contributors to skepticism. However, he firmly reassured Kenyans that the current electoral management framework leaves no room for rigging, asserting that the notion of electoral theft is no longer feasible in today’s environment. To further bolster public confidence, the Commissioner announced that IEBC will conduct practical live simulation exercises in media outlets demonstrating the voting and results management processes. These simulations intend to demystify the electoral process and clearly show how it is safeguarded against any interference. Commissioner Alutalala’s media engagements reaffirm the Commission’s resolve to deliver a credible, transparent, and inclusive electoral process in 2027.

title: IEBC engages security agents, targets peaceful, credible and secure elections14th Sep 2025
text: The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), led by its Chairperson, Erastus Edung Ethekon, 5th September, 2025 held a strategic engagement with security agencies from Mombasa, Kilifi, and Kwale Counties. The meeting sought to strengthen collaboration as the Commission embarks on key electoral activities, including the resumption of Continuous Voter Registration (CVR), the conduct of by-elections, and other planned operations within the electoral calendar. In his opening remarks, the Chairperson emphasized that the Commission’s responsibility goes beyond the administration of elections. “As a Commission, our duty goes beyond administering elections; it extends to safeguarding fairness, credibility, and peace in the electoral process,” he stated. He further noted that since 2013, IEBC has worked closely with national security agencies and other stakeholders under the Election Security Arrangement Programme (ESAP) a strategic coordination framework that has proven vital in maintaining electoral integrity and building public confidence. He lauded these partnerships, describing them as instrumental in delivering peaceful and credible elections. The Chairperson cited the 2022 Post-Election Evaluation Report, which reaffirmed the effectiveness of this collaboration, highlighting that ESAP significantly enhanced coordination between the Commission, the National Police Service, and other stakeholders. This, he noted, played a critical role in ensuring safe and peaceful elections across the country. Underscoring that election security is a continuous process, the Chairperson stressed that it spans the entire electoral cycle from voter registration, voter education, and campaigns to nominations, polling, tallying, results declaration, and even post-election activities.

title: Master trainers reviews training content for staff in readiness for resumption of Continuous Voter Registration exercise14th Sep 2025
text: The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) last week held a workshop to develop training content and methodology by Master Trainers ahead of the resumption of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) on 29th September, 2025. This will be followed by a comprehensive training for both field Registration Officers and support staff from the headquarters. The training will adopt a three-tier model. Tier 1 involves developing training content and methodology by Master Trainers, Tier 2 targets Training of Trainers (TOTs), and Tier 3 involves comprehensive training of field officers and support staff from headquarters. This programme will cover all aspects of the CVR process, from operational procedures to the technical nuances of the new Kenya Integrated Election Management System’s (KIEMS) voter registration module. The Commission notes that this approach will ensure consistency and standardization of electoral operations across all levels and offices of Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC). Further, it will provide uniform application of electoral laws, procedures, technologies and enhance preparedness and risk management aspects of the CVR exercise.

title: Commission engages Civil Society Organisations to build united front and strengthen electoral governance14th Sep 2025
text:
Last week marked a pivotal moment for Kenya’s democratic future as the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), led by Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW, held a high-level round-table meeting with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) under the Uchaguzi Platform, with support from ELOG and ELGIA.

With the 2027 General Election on the horizon, the meeting aimed to build a united front between the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission and civil society to strengthen electoral governance, promote transparency, and defend the sanctity of the vote.

Vice Chair Fahima, speaking on behalf of Chairperson Erestus Edung Ethekon, emphasized the Commission’s commitment to inclusive, participatory, and accountable elections.

“Your proposals will guide the development of policy and strategy to enhance participation and restore public trust in the electoral process,” she said.

The Commission also sounded the alarm on the growing threat of misinformation and disinformation, cautioningCSOs to stay vigilant against politically driven narratives that could undermine electoral integrity and national unity.

Representatives from Uchaguzi Platform, including Felix Odhiambo from ELGIA Africa and the National Coordinator of Elog-Mulle Musau, commended IEBC’s willingness to engage and pledged full support in advancing transparency, civic engagement, and accountability.

With democracy under pressure globally, Kenya is standing tall—fighting for a future where every vote counts and every voice matters. The 2027 journey starts now—and it’s a call to all patriots to guard our ballot and defend our democracy.

title: IEBC stand shines, scoops Best Independent Commission Stand Award at Mombasa International Show14th Sep 2025
text: The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) was honored with the Best Independent Commission Stand award at the Mombasa International Show which was held between 3rd to 7th of September 2025 in Mombasa, in recognition of its exceptional exhibition, informative displays, and voter education efforts. The award was officially presented to IEBC Chairperson, Mr. Erastus Edung Ethekon, by his excellecny the President Dr.William Samoe Ruto who received it on behalf of the Commission. The recognition celebrates IEBC’s ongoing commitment to educating the public, fostering transparency, and strengthening Kenya’s democratic processes through open, informative engagements. This year’s Mombasa International Show was held under the theme: “Promoting Climate Smart Agriculture & Trade Initiatives for Sustainable Economic Growth.” While the theme emphasizes agricultural and economic innovation, IEBC’s participation highlights the critical role inclusive and informed electoral processes play in achieving national development goals. The IEBC’s exhibition stand was designed to be interactive and educational, offering visitors the opportunity to: • Explore electoral equipment and technology • Participate in simulated voter registration and polling • Access voter education materials , voting procedures, and electoral reforms • Engage directly with IEBC officials and ask questions about electoral laws and upcoming events This setup provided a hands-on learning experience for citizens, especially youth and first-time voters. Following its success in Mombasa, the Commission will next participate in the Nairobi International Trade Fair (NITF), scheduled to take place from 29th September to 5th October 2025 at Jamhuri Show ground.

title: Commission participates in technical workshop to develop guidelines for Artificial Intelligence in elections9th Sep 2025
text: The Commission led by Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, is participated in a two-day Technical Workshop on Developing Guidelines for Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Elections convened by Yiaga Africa in Nairobi. Speaking during the workshop the Chairperson emphasized that AI is reshaping how societies govern, communicate and engage. From voter registration to results transmission, it offers incredible opportunities but we must also confront its risks to protect electoral integrity. The Chairperson underscored the challenge for EMBs to embrace innovation without compromising electoral integrity. “Africa must lead not only in adopting AI, but also in setting ethical guardrails to ensure technology works for our democracies not against them,” Ethekon said. He hailed the development of the draft guidelines as a bold and necessary step, demonstrating that African EMBs are not passive observers but proactive architects of future-proof electoral systems. The Commission Secretary/CEO, Marjan Hussein Marjan, MBS, who is a Technical Committee Member on the Development of Guidelines on AI Use in Elections Management in Africa noted that the workshop signals a pivotal shift in Elections Management. “AI is no longer theoretical — it is already influencing election management, public discourse and institutional trust. From deepfakes and synthetic media to algorithmic micro-targeting and disinformation networks, the electoral landscape is changing rapidly. EMBs must be ready — not only to respond but to lead,” Marjan said. The Executive Director of Yiaga Africa Mr. Samson Itodo expressed appreciation to the IEBC for cohosting the workshop and for its continued leadership and support. “This Technical Workshop provides a unique platform for countries, experts and stakeholders to review, refine, and validate the AI guidelines and to develop a comprehensive strategy for enhancing the capacity of EMBs in Africa to adopt and responsibly integrate AI into election management,” Itodo said. The IEBC Chairperson was accompanied by Commissioner Dr. Alutalala Mukhwana, Chair Voter Education, Partnerships, Communications and Stakeholder Engagement Committee. Other participants of the Workshop include Election Management Bodies (EMBs) in Africa who are members of the Working Group on AI and Elections in Africa including Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission of Kenya (IEBC), the Independent Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC), the Electoral Commission of Zambia, and the Electoral Commission of Cabo Verde. Also present are regional and continental stakeholders including the African Union, ECOWAS, the Electoral Commissions Forum of SADC Countries, ELOG, among other key partners.

title: IEBC pays courtesy call on Chief Justice, discuss areas of interest to impact 2027 GE9th Sep 2025
text: Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) Chairperson Erastus Ethekon and Members of the Commission on Wednesday 27th August, 2025 paid a courtesy call to the Chief Justice and President of the Supreme Court of Kenya, Hon. Lady Justice Martha Koome, EGH. The two institutions deliberated on matters of mutual interest that will impact the 2027 General Election. The Commission is seeking to strengthen mutual understanding and synergy between the two institutions and recognizes the critical role played by the Judiciary, specifically the Judiciary Committee on Elections (JCE), during the pre-election, election and post-election periods in ensuring fair and timely dispute resolution. The Chief Justice and members of the Supreme Court Hon. Justice Njoki Ndungu, CBS, who is also Chairperson of JCE, and Hon. Justice Daniel Musinga, Vice-Chairperson JCE, congratulated the IEBC Chairperson and Commissioners on their appointment to office and pledged to support them deliver on their mandate. The Chairperson noted that to strengthen the preparation for the 2027 General Election, the Commission proposes to revise electoral laws and Collaboration regulations to address challenges observed in 2017 and 2022. This will enhance collaboration with JCE to establish a more workable Electoral Dispute Resolution (EDR) framework, develop training programmes and curricula on electoral processes and dispute resolution. Further it will aid in building capacity of law enforcement agencies on electoral processes, strengthen stakeholder and government agency engagements and sensitize Judicial Officers on electoral processes, particularly the allocation of party lists.

title: Continuous voter registration to resume in September in preparation for 2027 GE9th Sep 2025
text: The Commission hereby announces that Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) will resume on Monday, 29th September 2025. This is in line with its constitutional mandate under Article 88(4) of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010. This exercise is a vital step in ensuring that every eligible Kenyan has the opportunity to participate in shaping the country’s future through democratic elections. It is particularly directed towards young people who have recently attained 18 years, and all citizens who have not yet registered or need to update their voter information. Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC noted that in readiness for the upcoming CVR exercise, the Commission has initiated a series of preparatory activities to ensure the process is efficient, inclusive, and transparent. These activities are critical for laying a strong foundation for a successful nationwide rollout. They include: Mapping of Registration Centres: Verifying both existing and proposed centres to ensure accessibility across the country. Stakeholder Engagements: Holding consultative forums at the constituency level to build awareness and promote participation. Geospatial Data Consolidation: Collecting constituency, county, and national-level data to guide resource planning. Preparation of Kenya Integrated Election Management System (KIEMS) Kits: Configuring and testing KIEMS kits. Gazettement of Officers: Official appointment of registration officers as required by law. Training of Registration Personnel: Equipping field officers with necessary skills for effective service delivery. Packaging and Distribution of Materials: Timely dispatch of registration materials to all operational areas. Data Protection Compliance: Conducting a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) to ensure full copliance with data protection laws. Voter Education Activities: Rolling out voter education programs to inform and engage the public. “Eligible Kenyans may register at any IEBC Constituency Office, except in areas currently with by-elections. Services available include new voter registration, transfer of voter registration to a new location, correction or update of voter details, and inspection of voter registration status,” said Ethekon.

title: Safeguarding Democracy - Curbing hate speech, disinformation in Kenya29th Aug 2025
text: As the nation prepares for the 2027 General Elections, hate speech and the spread of misinformation and disinformation stand out as urgent challenges that must be addressed. On 18th August 2025, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), led by Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, held a consultative meeting with the National Cohesion and Integration Commission (NCIC) to explore areas of collaboration. In his opening remarks, the IEBC Chairperson thanked NCIC for honoring the invitation, acknowledging the history of strong partnership between the two institutions and expressing optimism for continued cooperation. The meeting reaffirmed NCIC’s commitment to advancing national unity, eliminating ethnic discrimination, and promoting tolerance, diversity, and peaceful coexistence among Kenyans. Together, IEBC and NCIC underlined their shared responsibility to safeguard democracy, strengthen inclusivity, and promote peace across the country. Commissioner Ann Nderitu (IEBC) emphasized the importance of the “List of Fame and Shame” as one of the most effective tools in combating hate speech—recognizing responsible actors while exposing perpetrators. She stressed that this approach should be strengthened but cautioned that hate speech cannot be addressed in isolation. Collaboration between IEBC and NCIC is vital to pool resources, overcome budgetary challenges, and integrate anti-hate initiatives into broader civic education programs. “Working together, rather than in silos, will strengthen the fight against divisive rhetoric and reinforce public trust in democratic processes,” she added. Commissioner Dr. Danvas Makori (NCIC) highlighted the growing menace of misinformation and disinformation, describing them as “the greatest threat to democracy in the digital age.” He underscored that “You cannot win the minds of Kenyans until you win on misinformation and disinformation.” According to him, the solution lies in proactively providing citizens with accurate and timely information through robust social media monitoring, innovative communication strategies, and decisive countermeasures against false narratives that erode public confidence. Commissioner Hon. (Eng.) Phillip Okundi, EBS, HSC (NCIC) noted that the lack of trust in institutions has historically fueled tensions, sometimes culminating in violent elections. Breaking this cycle, he said, requires engaging Kenya’s Gen Z—not as passive observers but as active allies. As digital natives, they are uniquely positioned to challenge disinformation, champion transparency, and foster a culture of accountability. He further warned that Kenya continues to grapple with reconciliation and inclusivity deficits. Unfulfilled promises of the new constitution and political handshakes perceived as symbolic rather than unifying have deepened public cynicism. “Without genuine reconciliation, cycles of division and mistrust risk recurring—with dangerous consequences,” he said. IEBC Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Abdallah, OGW, raised concern over persistent societal challenges, particularly cyberbullying of women in leadership—often fueled by powerful actors—and cultural norms that discourage women’s political participation. Addressing these requires youth-focused education, deliberate empowerment of women leaders, and collective efforts to dismantle entrenched inequalities. NCIC Chairperson Rev. Dr. Samuel Kobia reiterated the Commission’s mandate: “NCIC is mandated to facilitate and promote equality of opportunity, good relations, harmony and peaceful co-existence between persons of different ethnic, religious and racial communities of Kenya, and to advise the Government on all aspects thereof.” IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon closed the meeting by reaffirming the need for a structured partnership: “We look forward to identifying key areas where NCIC and IEBC can collaborate under a clear framework of partnership, guided by a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). A top priority is election security—building on past successes and enhancing robust measures that safeguard electoral integrity and promote peace.”

title: IEBC holds introductory meeting with Political Parties Liaison Committee29th Aug 2025
text: The Commission led by Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, on 18th August, 2025 held an introductory meeting with the Steering Committee of the Political Parties Liaison Committee (PPLC), led by its Chairperson Evans Misati. In his opening remarks, Mr. Ethekon welcomed the PPLC leadership and underscored its indispensable role in the democratic process. “We are pleased to convene this session to identify areas of focus, address emerging concerns, and chart a way forward together,” he said. To enhance coordination with political parties, the IEBC Chairperson announced the appointment of Commissioner Marykaren Sorobit to oversee all matters relating to the PPLC. “Her leadership will be instrumental in ensuring that the Commission’s engagements with political parties are structured, responsive, and aligned with our broader electoral objectives,” he added. On his part, Evans Misati thanked the Commission for convening the meeting and emphasized the importance of collaboration between the PPLC and IEBC in strengthening Kenya’s electoral process. He urged the Commission to actively involve the PPLC in key activities such as voter registration, by-elections, general elections, and public sensitization. PPLC was established under Section 38 of the Political Parties Act, 2011 at both the national and county levels to provide a platform for structured dialogue between the Registrar of Political Parties, the Electoral Commission, and political parties. Its creation followed recommendations of the Kriegler Commission after the 2007 General Election. The Office of the Registrar of Political Parties has since sustained this dialogue framework through workshops and consultations. The PPLC seeks to champion free, fair, peaceful, and transparent electoral processes in Kenya, while promoting genuine interaction, experience sharing, and information exchange between political parties and the Electoral Management Body. It further identifies gaps in electoral law and practice and proposes reforms through a consultative approach. The committee was initially formed in 2009 following discussions between the Interim Independent Electoral Commission (IIEC), the Registrar of Political Parties, and 47 registered political parties, culminating in the Nakuru Resolutions of March 2010. Its official launch was completed on 21st October 2010, with Nairobi being the last region inaugurated. Today, the PPLC operates at both the national and county levels as a central platform for electoral dialogue.

title: Commission oversees conduct of AFC Leopards club elections28th Aug 2025
text: The Commission, through the Nairobi County office, midwifed the conduct of the AFC Leopards Sports CLub elections at Kasarani Stadium. The club’s Register had 2,706 eligible voters with 1,775 casting their ballot to make 65.91% voter turn out. The club held elections for the positions of Chairperson,Secretary General and Treasurer to steer the club for the next four (4) years. In the contest for the Club Chairperson, Boniface Ambani emerged the winner garnering 1,001 votes against his sole competitor Enoc Mutokah, who received 657 votes. In other positions, the winners were Mulindi Mulanda, who garnerd 656 to clinch the Secretary General position and Newton Lime, who won the treasurer position with 676 votes. The event for the first was peaceful and the candidates praised the IEBC for their professionalism and keen to details on election matters. Amosi Chilai, who served as the Returning Officer, encouraged other sports clubs to follow suit and use IEBC in their electoral activities.

title: Commission engages Mombasa based stakeholders to receive feedback and pursue collaboration on election process28th Aug 2025
text: The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) led by Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, who was accompanied by all Commissioners, on Wednesday 14th August, 2025 held a consultative meeting, on areas of mutual interest and collaboration, with Mombasa based civil society groups, community based organisations, special interest groups and social media influencers to enable the Commission deliver its mandate. The meeting provided a platform for dialogue, feedback and learning between the Commission and these important stakeholders. Ethokon said that the Commission will review the feedback received from the meeting to develop policy, improve strategy and enhance participation in the electoral processes. The Commission will also leverage on the stakeholders’ expertise and vital feedback to enhance participation of all citizens in the electoral activities throughout the three election phases – pre-election, election and post-election phases within the 5-year election cycle. “10th August 2027, may seem far — but election preparedness starts now. Let us promote elections that are peaceful, inclusive, and credible. “To influencers and bloggers: Use your platforms not just for products, but for nation-building....Let’s move from clickbait to truth-bait,” said the Chairperson. “To Gen Z champions: You are not just the future — you are the focus. “To civil society and media: We see you. We respect your watchdog role. Let’s keep engaging —constructively, boldly, and with purpose,” added Erastus Ethekon. The Chairperson thanked the stakeholders, describing them as the real heartbeat of public opinion in Kenya. He noted that their presence in today’s meeting spoke volumes. It showed that they care — not just about the next election — but about the future of our country. “Indeed, your voice matters now more than ever,” he summed up. The meeting provided a platform for dialogue, feedback and learning between the Commission and public benefiting organizations represented at the grassroot. The Commission will review the feedback received to develop policy, improve strategy and enhance participation in the electoral process. The Commission will also leverage on the stakeholder’s expertise to enhance participation of all citizens in the electoral activities throughout the three election phases – pre-election, election and postelection phases within the 5-year election cycle. Speaking at the same session, Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan Hussein Marjan, MBS noted that civil society actors, influencers, youth leaders and members of marginalized communities play a vital role in shaping public opinion, driving civic action and holding institutions accountable. “This meeting provides you the space to speak, share and shape how we move forward together. Use your words to build not to break. The Commission calls on you to support voter registration, voter education and prosperous Kenya. We all work towards that common goal peaceful and credible election and when you criticize us, we take positive criticism to improve Commission’s processes. “The Commission purpose is to protect Kenyan will to choose right leaders. Our media landscape is changing every day and our youth want news in real time and there is where your role as influencers is critical. You engage and interact with the youth on real time and your words are powerful,” he said. The Commission will provide framework, but every citizen is responsible to protect this space to have a peaceful election. Have trust in this Commission, they want to have a free and fair, credible election. Vice Chairperson Fahima Araphat Abdallah noted that the youth hold the largest voting bloc in Kenya and have their representation in the Commission. This demographic fact is a democratic force, because you hold the power to make a decision. Young people have power to significantly influence policy direction, but despite this huge number, youth participation in election remains negligible. “The youth must engage and inform participation. Youth seek factual and credible information on the electoral processes. Verify information to curb on the spread of fake news and misinformation in this era of technology and innovation. Use social media responsibly. Let us make informed participation in the electoral process,” she said. Further, the Commission seeks your collaboration to enable us have a peaceful election. Together we can champion inclusive representation, leverage technology positively. Participation in election is a responsibility, remember the story of Kenya democracy is still being written and the youth are the authors of the next chapter. Democracy thrives when its youngest citizen believe it. Let us believe and also live it.

title: Frequently Asked Questions -FAQs14th Aug 2025
text: IEBC – Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Public Communication | August 2025 When will voter registration begin? The Commission plans to commence continuous voter registration soon. The official start date will be communicated through IEBC’s website and verified social media channels. We encourage eligible voters to prepare to register or update their information once the process begins. How and when can I apply to be a polling clerk or election official for the by-elections? Currently, no recruitment is underway. The Commission will publicly advertise any vacancies on its official website, social media platforms, and in the media. Please keep checking for updates. How do I confirm whether I am registered as a voter? You can confirm your voter registration status by visiting: verify.iebc.or.ke What is the progress on the law to recall Members of Parliament? The Commission has made formal recommendations to Parliament to amend the Elections Act and address this legal gap. We remain hopeful that the necessary legal framework will be enacted to guide the recall of Members of Parliament. Is it currently possible to recall a Member of Parliament? Unfortunately, there is no enabling law that provides grounds or procedures for recalling MPs. However, for Members of County Assemblies (MCAs), the law exists, and the Commission will process valid recall petitions as guided by existing legislation. How do I transfer my voter registration to another area? Once continuous voter registration resumes, visit the IEBC office in the constituency you wish to transfer to. Bring the national ID or passport used during your initial registration. Why are the by-elections scheduled so far away from the vacancies being declared? While legal timelines guide the process, practical considerations such as the school calendar also play a key role. Many polling stations are located in schools. To avoid disrupting learning and national exams, the Commission scheduled the by-elections for 27th November 2025. Why do many Returning Officers seem to come from the same region (e.g. Rift Valley)? The Commission draws Returning Officers from its in-post staff, ensuring regional representation across all 290 constituencies as required by law. Staff are routinely rotated across the country to promote neutrality, fairness, and inclusivity. There is no ethnic or regional bias in these appointments. Are there any areas undergoing boundaries delimitation? The Commission is awaiting an advisory from the Supreme Court on the matter. While constitutional timelines for delimitation have passed, further direction from the court will inform the Commission’s next steps. Why are all Returning Officers in some areas (e.g. Kisii or Nairobi) from one community or region? All Returning Officers are existing IEBC staff members assigned based on operational needs. Officers are posted across counties to ensure impartiality and to avoid conflict of interest. These decisions are not based on ethnic, regional, or political considerations. Why are officials in places like Nyamira or Embakasi not from the local community? IEBC staff are deployed nationally to maintain neutrality and public confidence in the electoral process. Officers posted in these areas are trained and familiar with the local context and have served across regions in previous electoral cycles. What is IEBC’s position on accusations that returning officers are politically aligned? The Commission strongly affirms its independence and impartiality. Returning Officers are career civil servants within the institution, appointed without political influence and rotated regularly to prevent bias. Are the by-election dates compliant with Article 101(4)(b) of the Constitution? The Constitution mandates that by-elections be held within 90 days of a writ being issued. While the Commission is guided by this, logistical constraints such as school calendars must be taken into account. Many polling centers are located in schools, which will be in session during the initial 90-day period. Holding elections without access to polling centers is not practical. The new date aligns with both legal and logistical realities. Is IEBC supposed to officially announce the date of the next General Election? No. The Constitution already sets the date: Second Tuesday of August every fifth year. Therefore, the next General Election will be held on 10th August 2027. No separate announcement is required from the Commission. What is IEBC’s response to claims that nomination replacements (e.g. Hon. Mbadi’s case) were handled unlawfully? This matter is currently before the courts. In respect of the judicial process, the Commission will not comment further and will await the court’s decision. Why are some returning officers in places like Nairobi drawn from North Eastern or other distant regions? IEBC assigns its officers based on operational planning and fairness. Cross-posting ensures objectivity and guards against local biases or influence. Every region contributes staff who are then deployed nationwide, in line with the principles of national inclusivity. What is IEBC doing to combat misinformation and disinformation? The Commission recognizes the challenges of fake news, disinformation, and digital manipulation. We are actively working with civil society, digital influencers, and media to promote verified information and digital integrity. We urge the public to rely only on information shared through official IEBC platforms. Still have questions? Reach out to us: Email: info@iebc.or.ke Social Media: @IEBCKenya on X, Facebook, Instagram IEBC: Empowering Voters. Protecting Democracy. Your Vote, Your Voice, Your Future.

title: Speaker hosts Commissioners, discuss key areas of national importance7th Aug 2025
text: The National Assembly, led by the Speaker Moses Masika Wetang’ula, EGH, MP on Thursday 31st July, 2025 hosted Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) Chairperson Erastus Ethekon, HSC and Members of the Commission for a discussion on key areas of national importance. The Speaker congratulated the Chairperson and Members of the reconstituted IEBC following their assumption into office. Speaker Wetang’ula urged the Commission to move with speed to conduct inclusive stakeholder engagements to enhance the public’s confidence in the institution and uphold its rightful place as the cornerstone of free, fair, verifiable and credible elections. He noted that Kenyans expect impartiality, integrity and professionalism as the Commission discharges its Constitutional mandate. The Speaker further encouraged IEBC to reach out to the Parliament on matters electoral reforms ahead of the 2027GE through the Senate’s Justice, Legal Affairs and Human Rights (JLAHRC) Committee and the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Justice and Legal Affairs (JLAC). IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon, HSC emphasised that the Commission continues to grapple with significant challenges in fulfilling its mandate and ensuring the successful delivery of a credible, free, fair, inclusive and transparent 2027 General Election. The Chairperson underscored the growing threat of fake news cautioning that these digital disruptions may jeopardise the integrity of democratic processes not only in Kenya but across the globe. The Chairperson reaffirmed his unwavering commitment and that of his fellow Commissioners to uphold the Constitution and serve the nation with transparency, impartiality and integrity. He emphasized that the Commission’s dedication to fostering public trust and delivering credible electoral processes is grounded in inclusiveness and accountability. Further, the Chairperson appealed to the National Assembly for their continued support as the Commission strives to strengthen democratic institutions and foster a more just and accountable future for all Kenyans. “As per the Second Schedule of the IEBC Act, the Commission has established Committees for the conduct of its business. The Commission has also conducted election through party lists by filling one vacancy in the National Assembly and nine in the County Assemblies. The nominee to the NA has since assumed office,” said Ethokon. The Commission informed the Speaker that it is preparing to commence voter registration in August/ September and will conduct the 23 By-elections in October or November 2025. “The Commission has to date received 23 Notice of Vacancies. We expect the by- elections to be held by November. The Commission has also submitted proposals to Parliament on several bills and election related regulations for consideration. The Commission proposes that the said proposals be considered and enacted as they comply with Court Orders and emerging issues in the electoral legal framework,” added Ethokon. The Chairperson noted that the proposals on grounds for recall of Members of National Assembly and Senate have been submitted to Parliament awaiting consideration and enactment. Recall Clause on the Members of the County Assembly is operational. The Commission requested the National Assembly to consider issuance of writs in concurrence to timelines for conducting the impending by-elections. The Speaker was also requested to intervene and fast track in the enactment of the electoral legal proposals submitted to Parliament to enable the Commission to discharge its mandate accordingly. Additionally, the Commission asked the National Assembly to allocate Kshs. 228 million to cater for the seven additional by-elections, which have not been catered for in the current allocation. “Consider facilitating the frontloading of Kshs. 4.3 billion from FY2027/2028 to the current FY2025/2026 to cater for Commission priority needs such as purchase of KIEMS & related ICT items; conduct of enhanced continuous voter registration; conduct of voter education and communication activities; and purchase of motor vehicles,” said Ethokon. The Commission also requested for the National Assembly to increase the 2027 General Election budget by Kshs. 7.6 billion to cater for financial gaps created by recent budget cuts. This is besides allocating funds to offset pending bills worth Kshs. 5.8 billion.

title: UN Resident Coordinator pays courtesy call on Commission, renews collaboration7th Aug 2025
text: A United Nations delegation led by UN Resident Coordinator Dr. Stephen Jackson and UNDP Deputy Resident Representative – Programmes Madelena Monoja paid a courtesy call to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC). The delegation was welcomed by Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) Chairperson Erastus Ethekon together with Members of the Commission and discussed a raft of programmes and activities that UNDP can support and partner with the Commission. In particular, the Chairperson discussed voter registration exercise, pending by-elections and enhancing grassroot voter education. The Chairperson acknowledged the work done by the Secretariat in drafting the 2024-2029 Strategic Plan, from which the Commission will develop the Election Operation Plan (EOP) and the Boundaries Review Operation Plan (BROP). The delegation was also apprised on the induction programme that the Commissioners were taken through where they interacted with experts in governance, law and elections. The Chairperson acclaimed the induction as informative as it highlighted the challenges encountered from previous elections and best global practices. Chairperson recognised the role UNDP plays in Kenya’s electoral process and asked the development partners to continue supporting the Commission especially in the upcoming by-elections. The delegation shared its congratulatory messages on the appointment and swearing in of the Commission and pledged to continue supporting the Commission deliver on its mandate ahead of the 2027 General Election. UN Resident Coordinator Dr. Stephen Jackson said it was a pleasure to meet the new Commission noting that UNDP has had partnership with the Commission that has endured many electoral cycles and he was glad to renew the partnership now that the new Commission was in place.

text: EACC, ODPP Pledge Joint Action Against Corruption and Money Laundering The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) and the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP) have strengthened their partnership to improve the investigation and prosecution of corruption and money laundering cases. He noted that while each institution has a distinct constitutional mandate, they share a common responsibility to deliver justice through effective investigations, successful prosecutions, and the recovery of assets acquired through corruption. CEO, Mr. Abdi Mohamud, said the fight against corruption requires institutions across the justice sector to work together. Director of Public Prosecutions Mr. Renson Ingonga said the meeting provided an opportunity to strengthen cooperation between the two institutions and improve the quality of investigations and prosecutions.
