This was besides her conducting voter education sessions and mapping out the polling stations. “The students, teachers and parents were taken through voter education session where the RO emphasized on qualities of a good leader, roles of election officials, how to correctly mark a ballot paper, elections materials, and the general mandate of the Commission,” said Taabu. The School Elections Committee was mandated to carry out nomination and vetting of candidates, oversee the students’ campaigns, which were done after classes, play time and during school assemblies. There were four candidates who were cleared and presented for the presidential race. Other positions vied for were Cabinet Secretaries for health, debate, religion, games, environment, sanitation, dining hall and time keeper. The voter turnout on the election day was at 99.9 per cent. Suheil Amir was elected as the new school President with Naizal Khalfan picked as her deputy. The teachers served as Presiding Officers, Deputy Presiding Officers and clerks.

title: IEBC and FAWE engage young female leaders and aspirants in Machakos to discuss status of women political participation in Kenya23rd Aug 2024
text: The Commission on 14 -15 August, 2024 engaged young women leaders and aspirants in a workshop that discussed women political participation organized by the Forum for Africa Women Educationalists (FAWE). The workshop, which was held in Machakos, brought together participants drawn from Women Political in Participation (WPP) Academy with the objective to sensitize them on the Office of the Registrar of Political Parties (ORPP) processes and IEBC electoral processes. The Women in Political Participation (WPP) project is a Pan-African gender project focused on the different facets of women and politics in Africa. Funded by the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, (SIDA) and implemented by International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance (Intenational IDEA), it aims to contribute to advancing the goal of gender equality in politics and governance, in line with the Maputo Protocol of 2003; various associated sub-regional protocols and standards, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The Constitution of Kenya, 2010 recognizes the rights of women to participate in elections. Specifically, Article 27 (3) notes that women have the right to equal treatment with men, including the right to equal opportunities in political, economic and social activities. Article 90 of the Constitution makes a deliberate effort to enhance the representation of women in parliament and county assemblies under the party list election framework. Further, article 27(8) requires the State to take legislative and other measures to implement the principle that not more than two-thirds of the members of elective or appointive bodies shall be of the same gender. In his speech Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan H. Marjan, MBS underlined the committed done over time to boost women participation in politics including adoption of a raft of deliberate measures that include the development and implementation of a gender and social inclusion policy that provides strategic direction on inclusion in the electoral process. The Commission also reduced by half the nomination fees paid by women candidates, rejected party nomination lists that are non-compliant with the not more two-thirds gender principle and enforced the Code of Conduct during the Campaign period and constitutes committees that hear, determine and penalize candidates and political parties that perpetrate electoral malpractice including disenfranchisement of women candidates’ political rights. “There is a notable increase in the number of women candidates who vied for the six elective seats during the 2022 General Election, where a total of 1,964 women out of 16,098 candidates registered to contest for the 1,882 vacant seats across the country in 2022. This was an improvement from the 1,359 out of the total 14,552 candidates, who vied during the 2017 General Election. “The number of women elected to leadership positions also increased from 172 in 2017 General Election to 201 in the 2022 General Election besides having a woman, for the first time, nominated and cleared by a majority party to contest as Deputy President candidate,” said Marjan. Currently there are 7 women Governors elected as opposed to 3 in 2017. The number of women elected as Members of the National Assembly has grown to 30 (2022) from 23 in 2017 while there are 114 women elected in the County Assemblies from 96 in 2017. Though number of women named in political party nomination is still dismissal, statistics from the Commission’s Register of Voters show that out of the 22,120,458 voters registered for the 2022 General Election, women represent 49.12% being 10,862,268 and men represent 50.88%. This was an improvement compared to the 2017 General Election where we had 19,600,000 registered voters of which 46.6% were women Some of the hurdles women need to overcome to optimally enjoy political mileage include universal challenges barring women from participating in elections aligned to societal norms, cultural trends and stereotypes. Besides, women are less empowered resource-wise and lack adequate time compared to their male counterparts. Other hurdles include none responsiveness to the Gender supportive policies and legal frameworks by duty bearers, gender-based violence has been sophisticated and entrenched over the years due to the fluid technological advancements. This is addition to seeing women candidates harassed during nominations and campaign periods. To remedy theses constraints, there is need to explore funding opportunities to finance women candidates’ campaigns, enhance capacity building of women candidates especially at the grassroots to equip women with the requisite skills to favourable compete against their male counterparts. There is need to invoke constitutional/legal reforms to embed gender quotas, reservations and affirmative actions to ensure progressive attainment of the not more than two-thirds gender principle. Place accountability demands on political parties to enhance women political participation and representation in their ranks. Make party lists for nomination begin with a female candidate followed by a man in all the categories. Build confidence among women in the male dominated arena to end stereotypes attached to some positions. The Commission was represented by Joyce Ekuam, Manager Partnerships and Stakeholder Engagement, Ruth Makuthu, the Ag. Manager Ag. Manager Legal Reforms, Political Parties and Campaign Financing and Linus Onyango, Risk Risk and Election Security Officer.

title: IEBC oversees conduct of Mountain View School Student Council election in Roysambu23rd Aug 2024
text: The Commission was called upon to conduct the Mountain View School Students' Council election, which were held on 19th July, 2024. The school is located in Roysambu Ward, Roysambu Constituency within Nairobi County has a student population of 1535. Notable landmarks near the school includes Safari Park hotel and USIU. The School is divided into three sections - Lower Primary, Upper Primary and Junior Secondary School. The Commission agreed to engage the school and conduct its students council election in order to inculcate the culture of democracy and encourage the students to participate in future elections once they attain the majority age. Several meetings were held between the school election committee and Roysambu Constituency IEBC office to plan for the activities preceding the election, which included nomination of candidates, voter education, election materials logistics and the actual voting. During the meetings, it was agreed that the school election committee would conduct nomination and vetting of candidates and oversee the campaigns while the Commission was to conduct voter education prior to the election day, provide election materials and supervise the electoral process. The School had seven elective posts, which included: Three Presidents and their running mates for each section Three Dining hall Captains and their deputies for each section Governors for each Grade Three Environmental captains and their deputies for each section Three Sports Captains and their deputies for each section Three Young Catholics and three Christian union representatives for each section Forty Class secretaries During the meetings, it was agreed that the positions for Governors and Class secretaries was to be conducted manually while election of the other positions were to be done electronically through the use of tablets to be provided by the school. Roysambu Constituency Senior Election Officer was named the Returning Officer assisted by Rachel Mariga the AEO. Each polling station had one Presiding Officer and a deputy, who were to be teachers, three clerks from the student’s population, one agent for each candidate while the parents body provided media and observers. The election was held between 09:00 and 14:00 hours and there was an impressive 99.9% voter turnout. This high level of participation demonstrated the students’ strong engagement and interest in the School’s leadership and activities.

title: USAID Kenya Democratic Governance Peace and Security Office pays courtesy call to IEBC23rd Aug 2024
text: The Commission held a meeting with officials from the USAID Kenya and East Africa's Democratic Governance Peace and Security Office. Led by Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan H. Marjan, MBS the Commission welcomed the vsitors who are currently holding consultative meetings with key electoral stakeholders to gain deeper understanding of what worked and what did not work well during the 2022 General Electoral and to identify stakeholders' priorities before, during and after the 2027 electoral cycle. The meeting was aimed to inform USAID's programming and support for the 2027 General Elections. Marjan welcomed the USAID team and acknowledged their support during the 2022 General Elections through various partners, including IFES, UNDP, ELGIA, and URAIA Trust. He highlighted the Commission's achievements, such as training, risk management, and public outreach, made possible through these partnerships. Representatives from the Commission, including Ruth Kulundu, DCS- Operations, DLS, DICT, Ag. DVEP, Ag. DSCM, MCPA, MEO, and MRM shared their achievements and challenges during the 2022 General Election and outlined areas where they require support in the current electoral cycle. Elizabeth Kilema, Project Management Specialist for Democracy and Elections led the USAID team and thanked the Commission for the meeting. She emphasized the Commission's critical role in governance and democracy and expressed USAID's commitment to continuous support. Kilema said that USAID has worked with the Commission through partner organizations in the past, however, they are looking to establish more direct and organized collaborations to understand the Commission's needs better and provide tailored support. The USAID team has expressed interest in engaging further with the Commission to strengthen the partnership.

title: Commission submits to PAC in response to Auditor General queries on 2021/22 accounts23rd Aug 2024
text: The Commission appeared before the Parliamentary Accounts Committee (PAC) on July 29, 2024, to address the Auditor General's queries on its Financial Statements for FY 2021/2022. Led by Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan H. Marjan, MBS, the team made submission to the Committee, which had sought clarification on several historical issues, including the status of inherited Election Commission of Kenya (ECK) land and motor vehicle valuation and ownership documents. The Committee also sought clarity on the long outstanding funds receivables from the National Treasury with regards to salary advances, imprests and car loan recoveries from officers and Commissioners of the defunct ECK, pending bills, and the Commission's progress in adopting the Inventory Management System.

title: IEBC submits before Senates JLAC as part of public participation process on five Bills23rd Aug 2024
text: The Commission made submissions to the Senate’s Committee on Justice, Legal Affairs and Human Rights (JLAC) on five Bills as part of the public participation process to collect views and comments from the relevant stakeholders. The submissions were presented before Senate’s JLAC on July 22nd and 29th, 2024. The Bills were the County Governments Election Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024 (Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 35 (Senate Bills No. 2). The Bill seeks to ensure that at least five percent of the members of a County Assembly are representatives of Persons Living with Disabilities (PWDs) in line with the provisions of Article 54(2) of the Constitution of Kenya. The Elections Offences (Amendment) Bill, 2024 (Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 98 (Senate Bills No. 28). This Bill seeks to amend section 6 of the Election Offences Act to introduce additional offences that may be committed by a member and staff of the Commission: - conducting an election in an ungazetted polling station; - unreasonably delaying the declaration of election results; and - altering declared election results The Political Parties (Amendment) Bill, 2024 (Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 96 (Senate Bills No. 26). This Bill seeks to inter alia amend the Political Parties Act to replace the Office of Registrar of Political Parties with the Independent Political Parties Regulatory Commission and to provide clarity on provisions raising ambiguity. The Elections (Amendment) Bill, 2024 (Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 99 (Senate Bills No. 29) seeks among others to amend the Elections Act, 2011 and provide clarity on provisions raising ambiguity. It adds provisions touching on the conduct of elections generally with a focus on voter eligibility and registration, and candidate eligibility and nomination. The Bill also addresses related matters on political party regulation and pre-election dispute resolution in respect to nomination of candidates for elections. It seeks to provide clarity on ICT in elections regarding transmission of election results and the process of collation, announcement and declaration of results from the polling stations to the Tallying Centers also stands key in addressing the result path within the conduct of elections. Finally, the County Boundaries Bill, 2023 (Senate Bill No. 6 of 2023), which under Article 188 of the Constitution provides a constitutional platform on which the boundaries of a county may be altered, upon a resolution recommended by an Independent Commission set up for that purpose and passed by both the National Assembly and the Senate. The County Boundaries Bill, 2023 seeks, among others, to define the boundaries of Kenya, provide the legal framework for the resolution of county boundary disputes through the establishment of a county boundaries mediation committee and to give effect to Article 188 of the Constitution on the alteration of county boundaries The Commission, being one of the critical stakeholders, made submissions to JLAC to align with Article 118(1)(b) of the Constitution of Kenya,2010, and National Assembly Standing Order 127(3), which mandate Parliament to ensure public participation and involvement in legislative processes and committee business. The Commission presented its views on all the Bills aimed at amending existing electoral laws in Kenya and is part of ongoing efforts to reform and improve the electoral framework in the country. In addition, the Commission appeared by the Parliamentary Committee on Justice and Legal Affairs of the National Assembly and made submissions on the proposed County Boundaries Bill, 2023. Other institutions present during the submissions were NGEC, ORPP, PPLC, Council of Governors, County Assemblies Forum, National Youth Council, FIDA Kenya, Elog, Mzalendo Trust, Inter-religious Council of Kenya, Katiba Institute, Transparency International, Comptroller of Budget, Intergovernmental Relations Technical committee and National Council for Persons with Disability.

title: Commission appears before National Assemblys JLAC, presents Supplementary Budget Estimates29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission appeared before the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Justice & Legal Affairs (JLAC) on 17th July 2024 to submit the 2024/2025 Supplementary Budget estimates. The meeting, which was chaired by Tharaka Constituency member of National Assembly, Hon. George Murugara who chairs the Committee, saw the Commission outline key funding priorities areas that are crucial for the sustenance of the it's operations. The IEBC team was led by Deputy Commission Secretary – Operations Ruth Kulundu accompanied by members of senior management. The primary focus of the meeting was for the Commission to emphasize critical areas that require financial facilitation to ensure that the Commission's continue to function effectively. some of the notable areas that the Commission highlighted for funding include settlement of pending bills, election technology, medical insurance among others. DCS Kulundu while presenting the budget estimates to the committee, justified the budget items and underscored the importance of the National Treasury to fund the proposed budget lines to enable the Commission to deliver on its mandate and enhance its operational capacity.

title: IEBC presides over election of Directors for Smallholder Tea Factories in Kenya29th Jul 2024
text: On the 28th and 29th June, 2024, the Commission conducted elections for directors of 54 smallholder tea factories across 14 counties in Kenya. The election was a result of court order requiring the Tea Board of Kenya (TBK) to oversee the election of directors for these factories. To guarantee credibility of the process, TBK engaged the Commission to conduct the elections. The Commission signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the TBK as well as each of the 54 Smallholder Tea Factories to undertake these elections. The elections were conducted by secret ballot, to guarantee secrecy of the ballot as well as ensure security of the voters' choices. The Commission deployed well-trained personnel to oversee the electoral process, ensuring adherence to the highest standards of electoral integrity. The successful conduct of these elections marks a significant milestone in the governance of smallholder tea factories in Kenya. The choice of IEBC was also a nod in the trust institutions have in the EMB and we hope more organizations can take advantage of the Commission’s experience and stellar record in organizing and managing their elections. All the 54 small tea factories took part in the election where 334,162 farmers turned out to vote representing 52.19% voter turnout. "This is the first that tea farmers elections was conducted by a national, proffessional and independent body. This enabled farmers to exercise their democratic right in a transparent system of one farmer, one vote through a secret ballot. The IEBC successfully conducted the elections on the 28th and 29th June, 2024 in all the 54 tea factories," said Linturi while announcing the results on 2nd July, 2024. The former Cabinet Secretary for Agriculture and Livestock Development thanked the Commission for conducting the elections in a free fair transparent and credible manner.

title: IEBC hosts Somaliland NEC, shares election experience ahead of their Presidential and Legislative polls in November29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission met with the Somaliland National Electoral Commission (NEC) to share experiences in how to conduct credible elections ahead of the Presidential and Legislative polls in Somaliland set for November 2024. Deputy Commission Secretary – Operations Ruth Kulundu, who represented the Commission Secretary and CEO Marjan H. Marjan thanked the NEC for choosing Kenya to benchmark and learn more on technical support for the November 2024 elections. Kulundu stated that the Commission will assist the NEC to conduct successful elections. Moreover, she expressed gratitude to the NEC for their confidence in the IEBC adding that Kenya and Somaliland EMBs will have the opportunity to exchange ideas and experiences through this partnership to improve governance and democracy by holding credible elections. Musa Hassan, Chairman of the Somaliland National Elections Committee, thanked the Commission for agreeing to provide technical assistance to Somaliland as they prepare for the November 2024 elections. He emphasised that an earlier visit to IEBC, which was at the start of the year was critical as it taught them important lessons that have been crucial in the preparation of the November 2024 elections. Musa added that NEC is keen to sign an MoU with IEBC, which will ensure the two institutions have a solid framework to support each other beyond the November 2024 elections. NEC is also looking forward to have IEBC technical staff visit Somaliland and provide on-site training and support to NEC staff. He appreciated the experience sharing and valuable lessons learned from the various presentations made, and anticipates more engagements ahead of the elections. The Somaliland Ambassador to Kenya, H.E. Dr. Mohamed Ahmed Mohamoud, expressed gratitude to the Commission for agreeing to support the NEC to carry out credibility elections. Mohamed noted that the ideas shared will be useful in the run-up to the elections and held Somaliland. Strengthen its democracy. “IEBC played a critical role to set high standards in election management, which other EMBS in the region and around the world should emulate. IEBC has put in place transparent electoral processes,” said Ambassador Mohamoud. IEBC has pledged to offer technical support in a number of areas in the electoral process including voter education and training, supply chain management, voter verification and registration, election monitoring and observation as requested by NEC. Other IEBC representatives present at the meeting included DICT, DLS, Ag. DVEP, Ag. DREB&RM, Ag. DSCM, MCPA, and MPA-CS/CEO, as well as the Somaliland NEC Vice Chairman and Commissioners and the Somaliland Deputy Ambassador to Kenya.

title: National Treasury trains Commission staff on new electronic government procurement and inventory management systems29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission in collaboration with The National Treasury and ELGIA is holding a 3-day training workshop on the new electronic government procurement system (e-GP), Inventory Management System (IMS) and procurement litigation. The e-G is set to be used by all government entities in the country starting 1st July 2024. The aim of the system is to make procurement easier and faster. Opening the workshop, the Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan Hussein Marjan applauded The National Treasury for taking time to train and ensure the Commission staff are familiar with the new procurement system. He also thanked ELGIA for supporting the training.

title: IEBC renews collaboration with UCSPAK to strengthen students role in electoral process29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission today hosted the leadership of the Universities College Students Peace Association of Kenya (UCSPAK), discussed mutual areas for collaboration and resigned the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen their work relationship. Deputy Commission Secretary - Operations Ruth Kulundu emphasized the Commission's positive working relationship with UCSPAK, particularly in mobilizing their members to participate in electoral processes. Allan Chacha, CEO of UCSPAK, acknowledged the Commission as a crucial stakeholder that has supported good governance in University Student Leader elections through mentorship. He noted that as UCSPAK prepares to unveil its strategic plan later this year, the partnership will enhance youth participation in electoral processes since governance is one of its key pillars. Chacha expressed UCSPAK's intent to strengthen their partnership with the Commission. Under the Governance Pillar the Commission will lead in mentorship of student leaders and aspiring leaders, voter registration, voter education, election observation, boundaries delimitation to equip university students with the electoral processes. Ag. DVEP, Amina Soud, HSC observed that the IEBC–USPACK relationship has been successful and the renewing of the MoU will strengthen future collaboration.

title: IEBC conducts data collection and analysis principles training for M and E champions29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission, with support from the International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES), is holding a data collection and analysis principles approaches workshop for the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Champions. The training and capacity assessment workshop is aimed at enabling the Commission hinge its policy decisions on data collected to inform the electoral process. Deputy Commission Secretary – Operations Ruth Kulundu, who presided over the opening ceremony of the workshop, noted that institutions need data to make decisions, which is crucial to the Commission. Data informs and the Commission has acquired data such as number of youth, women, minorities and PWDs involved in conduct of the electoral processes and should utilize it to inform its decisions. “We thank IFES for the support received so far, and pledge to work hand in hand and attain more through collaboration. We will work closely to see areas to prioritise and ask IFES to support,” said Ruth Kulundu. IFES Country Director - Kenya, Obaje Ukeh observed that data is utilized to inform decisions. He said the workshop is just a start in the collaboration between IEBC and IFES to build capacity of Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) in the Commission. “Every department in the Commission should be able to utilize MEL to assess its performance,” he said.

title: Gender and equality Commission tours IEBC offices to discuss 2022GE recommendations29th Jul 2024
text: The National Gender and Equality Commission-Kenya today paid a courtesy call to the IEBC and discussed the 2022GE post election monitoring recommendations. The team was received by Ruth Kulundu, IEBC Deputy Commission Secretary (DCS) - Operations, who said that the Commission is committed to delivering free, fair, transparent, credible and inclusive elections, that ensure participation and engagement of Special Interest Groups (SIGs) throughout the electoral cycle. “NGEC monitored participation and engagement of Special Interest Groups (SIGs) during the 2022 General Election. The findings and key recommendations are contained in the report dubbed "Involvement and Participation of Special Interest Groups (SIGS) in the 2022 General Elections in Kenya,” said Mr. Paul Kuria, Ag. Commission Secretary/CEO NGEC. The report has not only assessed election preparedness and involvement of SIGs as candidates, voters, agents and observers of elections; but it has also documented incidences of gender-based violence and response, violence against women, and inequalities and discrimination encountered by SIGs in the election processes. “IEBC is considering recommendations from our stakeholders as outlined in the #2022GE Post Election Evaluation Report and Election Observation Reports, with the goal of improving the electoral processes”, said Kulundu, IEBC DCS - Operations. Mr. Kuria thanked the Commission for heeding the call for a meeting and taking into account NGEC’s recommendations with a goal of mutual collaboration to improve participation of the SIGs in elections.

title: Commission holds security briefing in Nyeri,  Kericho ahead of tea factories directors polls29th Jul 2024
text: IEBC and Ministry of Interior & National Administration participated in security briefing meetings organized by the Tea Board of Kenya (TBK). The meetings, which took place in Nyeri and Kericho counties on Friday, brought together security officers from 7 and 8 counties respectively, in the tea growing areas. The meetings discussed the significance of security and administrative coordination in elections for Directors of 54 smallholder tea factories scheduled for 28 June 2024. In Nyeri, Mr. Jacktone Nyonje, IEBC Manager for Electoral Training, provided an update on the level of preparedness for the elections. He reiterated that the elections for Directors of 54 smallholder tea factories will be conducted in a free, fair and credible manner. In addition, the Nyeri County Election Manager, Anastacia Mutua, underscored the importance of collaboration with security officers, highlighting the crucial role they played in the 2022 General Election. “These elections mark a significant milestone in the Tea Reforms Transformation journey. Our aim is to instill good corporate governance, transparency and accountability within Kenya's smallholder tea sub-sector under the Tea Act 2020,” said the TBK Chairman, Mr. Jacob Kamau Kahiu.

title: Commission trains CEMs and ROs to oversee smallholder tea factories directors elections29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission in collaboration with Tea Board of Kenya (TBK) held a workshop to train County Election Managers, Returning Officers and Deputy Returning Officers from 14 counties that are home to smallholder tea factories managed by the Kenya Tea Development Agency (KTDA). The officers are preparing for the upcoming elections for the directors of 54 smallholder tea factories. This initiative follows a court order that requested the TBK to oversee the election of directors for Smallholder Tea Factories and KTDA. To ensure the execution of these court directives, TBK engaged the Commission to conduct these elections scheduled for 28th June 2024. During the opening ceremony of the workshop, Mr. Willy K. Mutai, CEO of the Tea Board of Kenya, emphasized the significance of these elections in the broader context of tea sector reforms. “These elections mark an important milestone in the Tea Reforms Transformation journey aimed at inculcating good corporate governance within the smallholder tea sub-sector in Kenya,” he said. Deputy Commission Secretary - Operations, Ruth Kulundu, expressed gratitude to TBK for the opportunity to conduct these elections. She highlighted the collaborative commitment of both institutions to ensure a transparent and credible electoral process for the leadership of smallholder tea factories, which is crucial to Kenya’s tea industry. During the closing ceremony, Commission Secretary/CEO, Marjan H. Marjan observed that IEBC was glad to establish robust structures, comprehensive documentation, and clear processes and procedures for the Tea Factory elections. Safeguarding the integrity and success in these elections is our top priority. We extend our gratitude to the Tea Board of Kenya for their invaluable support and cooperation throughout our training workshop. Together, we are making significant strides towards a successful election," he said. Later, IEBC met officials from Kenya Tea Development Agency - Holdings Limited, Tea Board of Kenya and Ministry of Interior and National Administration for a consultative meeting chaired by Cabinet Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development, Hon. Mithika Linturi, EGH to discuss modalities on the conduct of elections. Marjan H. Marjan, MBS, IEBC Commission Secretary/ CEO, reiterated the Commission’s commitment to conduct free, fair and credible elections. “We express our confidence in IEBC’s ability to deliver a free, fair and transparent election as demonstrated in the 2022 General Election,” said Hon. Mithika Linturi, EGH, Cabinet Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development.

title: IEBC meets donor partners to review work plan, timeline for projects under Basket Fund29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission led by Deputy Commission Secretary (DCS) Support Service, Obadiah Keitany, who represented the Commission/CEO Marjan H. Marjan, MBS co-chaired the 9th Project Steering Committee meeting alongside implementing partners from UNDP, UNWomen, UN Human Rights - Office in Kenya, European Union, Germany Ambassy, Embassy of Ireland and Italian Embassy in Kenya. The meeting, which was held on on 29th May, 2024, sought to receive an approval of the revised annual work plan, new timelines and review the status report of the projects under the Basket Fund. UNDP Kenya Deputy Resident Representative - Programme Madelena Monoja noted that the project, which started in 2021 to support elections in Kenya, has had numerous achievements, which enabled IEBC to conduct a credible 2022 General Election that was peaceful, inclusive and countered misinformation and propaganda throughout the election cycle The Commission expressed its appreciation for the support received from the Development Partner’s Basket Fund as it was pivotal in ensuring that IEBC discharges its mandate The Commission is currently seeking support to review the strategic plan 2020-2024, which will inform the development of Strategic Plan 2024-2028 & the 2027 Election Operations Plan; rolling out of the paralegal training project; conduct of online voter registration and education and peer learning on electoral legal framework and election technologies. Further this support will be channeled to the establishment of Commission's technology testing, scrutiny and training lab.; establishment of a Customer Experience Centre- preliminary operations and piloting; development of career progression guidelines and acquisition of the fact checking tools to address mis/disinformation such as iVerify, iMonitor+ tool. The Commission is also keen to ensure all supported activities are duly implemented, and results shared as planned.

title: IEBC present as UCSPAK unveils 2024-28 Strategic Plan, highlights key result areas29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission on Friday joined the University and Colleges Students’ Peace Association of Kenya (UCSPAK) as they unpacked their 2024-2028 Strategic Plan to stakeholders, which included highlighting their key result areas. The Deputy Commission Secretary - Operations, Ruth Kulundu, applauded UCSPAK for partnering with IEBC especially in undertaking voter education among the youth. She reiterated that the Commission would continue to collaborate with UCSPAK and other stakeholders as it undertakes its mandate. UCSPAK is a non-political student association established with the major objective of fostering peace and good governance in institutions of higher learning in Kenya.

title: Commission makes submissions to Senate JLACs on IEBC (Amendment) Bill, 202429th Jul 2024
text: The IEBC led by the Commission Secretary, Marjan H. Marjan, MBS on Friday appeared before the Senate Committee on Justice, Legal Affairs and Human Rights (JLAC) to make submissions on the IEBC (Amendment) Bill, 2024 (National Assembly Bill No. 10 of the 2024). The IEBC presented its views on Sections 2 (Interpretation); 7A (Vacancy in the office of Chairperson and members); 10 (Secretary to the Commission); 36 (Procedure for delimitation of electoral boundaries); First Schedule (Procedure for appointment of Chairperson and Members of the Commission), Second Schedule (Provisions of conduct of the business and affairs of the Commission) and Fifth Schedule (Provisions relating to boundary delimitation) of the IEBC Act considering emerging reforms.

title: Somalia Prime Minister pays courtesy call on Commission, learns Kenyas electoral process29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission on Wednesday, May 8, 2024 hosted a delegation from the Federal Republic of Somalia led by Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre. The delegation was in the country benchmarking on various areas of interest including election management ahead of its country’s elections set for June 2024. In particular, the Somalia delegation was keen to learn how the Commission conforms to the principles of good governance while undertaking its mandate. The Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan H. Marjan welcomed the delegation and appreciated them for their recognition of the role the Commission plays in promoting democracy in Kenya. Somalia Prime Minister noted that Kenya’s election management body has proved to be instrumental in steering the country through electoral legal reforms and lauded IEBC for its commitment to conduct and supervise elections, carry out verifiable voter registration, undertake voter education and settle electoral disputes, which have set the bar high in Africa and the world. The Commission has shown professionalism and hinged its operations on the Constitution of Kenya. Somalia is keen to learn as it strives to strengthen its democratic processes despite the challenges it faces,” said Somalia PM Hamza Abdi Barre. The delegation was taken through the electoral processes, especially how the Commission has leveraged on electoral technology to carry out biometric voter registration, inspection and verification of register of voters, and results transmission to enhance credibility of Kenya’s elections.

title: Commission receives Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela delegations on benchmarking visit29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission hosted the Charge D’ Affairs from the Embassy of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela led by Counselor C'esar A. Chavarri C. who visited IEBC to seek collaboration and partnership in the electoral process. The team was met by Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan H. Marjan who took the opportunity to commend the Venezuelan delegation for choosing to visit the Commission, a move he said was a global endorsement of the work done by IEBC. “It is an honour for you to visit us. We take this gesture seriously and as an endorsement of our operations in conducting election and developing Kenya’s democratic process,” said Marjan. The Venezuelan team extended an invite to the Commission to be part of the Observer Mission during the upcoming elections in the South American state. The Venezuelan Presidential Election will be held on 28 th July 2024. Marjan highlighted the Commission operations and processes to the Venezuelan team and added that it is privileged to have Venezuelan EMB and other institutions visit IEBC for benchmarking and consultation. Noting that the invite will grant IEBC another chance to learn from a different scenario as the Venezuelan electoral system is different from the Kenya system. “There will be a lot to learn from the election observation mission to strengthen the electoral processes in the 2027 General Election,” said Marjan. The CEO was accompanied by the Deputy Commission Secretary (DCS) Support Services Mr. Obadiah Keitany, Michael Ouma, the Director ICT, Abdi Malim Ag. Director Voter Registration and Election Operation (DVREO) and Purity Njeru, Manager Communication and Public Affairs. The Charge D’ Affairs, commended the Commission for the exemplary work in elections management and noted his gratitude for the courtesy call. “This is the first step in opening up collaboration between Kenya and the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela on matters elections. The observation mission from Kenya will give the Commission an opportunity to learn from the Venezuelan National Election Council and exchange ideas with their counterpart which will be mutually beneficial to promote good governance and democracy,” he said.

title: IEBC Wajir team leads in county National Tree Growing Day, plants trees at the local Airbase29th Jul 2024
text: In Wajirs County, the Commission inn collaboration with stakeholders including Wajir County Government, Wajir County Security team, Kenya Human Rights Commission joined other citizens in the National Tree Growing Day to plant trees at the Wajir Airbase. This was part of the National Tree Growing Day exercise that was conducted countrywide to remember the lost lives of Kenyan citizens during the ongoing floods. Additionally, the tree growing exercise was meant to protect the environment and mitigate against the effects of climate change. The activity further enabled IEBC Wajir team led by Abdibashir Alinoor Ibrahim the Ag. CEM Wajir to engage stakeholders in enhancing our Corporate Social Responsibility within the local community.

title: IEBC joins Kenyans to mark National Tree Growing Day, plants trees in Ngong Road Forest, Bomas Block29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission led by Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan H. Marjan, MBS on Friday may 10th 2024 joined Kenyans in marking the National Tree Growing Day by planting trees at the Ngong Road Forest, Bomas Block, as part of the efforts to protect the environment and mitigate against the effects of climate change. The choice of this location rings a bell to many Kenyans because Bomas of Kenya, during the electioneering period, is synonymous with the Commission as it serves as the National Tallying Centre. The Commission is proud to join other Kenyans to make a positive contribution to our planet earth and support the national goal of increasing Kenya’s forest cover through planting 15 billion trees by 2032. Importantly, the Commission stands in solidarity with Kenyans who are affected by the floods and condoles with the families that lost their loved ones occasioned by the continuing floods being experienced in the country. Today is not only about tree planting, but also an opportunity to create awareness in our workplaces, families and society on the importance of environmental conservation and why the country needs to meet its target of increasing forest cover. The Commission has undertaken over 25 tree growing exercises across the country and continues to collaborate with relevant institutions to support efforts towards maintaining the planted trees so as to ensure they grow to maturity. These trees, planted with care and foresight, will not only benefit the current generation but will also stand as a legacy for future generations to cherish and protect.

title: IEBC, State Department for Diaspora Affairs meet to discuss diaspora community progress in polls29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission led by Deputy Commission Secretary (DCS) - Operations Ruth Kulundu today held discussions with the State Department of Diaspora Affairs led by Amb. Ann Wanjohi, the Director Liaison and Partnerships at the State Department of Diaspora Affairs to enhance the progressive participation of the diaspora community in the democratic process. The meeting also discussed how to facilitate voting for Kenyan citizens in the diaspora, voter registration for diaspora voters, voter education for Kenyans living in Diaspora, overview of the Commission plans and strategies for enhancing diaspora participation in election, exchange of information on polling stations for diaspora voting, fostering inclusive democratic processes in exploring avenues to increase participation in the democratic affairs and diaspora community engagement in the electoral process. <pstyle="margin: 0;"=""> DCS Kulundu, reiterated the importance of collaborating with the State Department for Diaspora Affairs to ensure Kenyans living in the diaspora are involved in the electoral process. Amb. Ann Wanjohi, the Director Liaison and Partnerships at the State Department of Diaspora Affairs, thanked the Commission for their conduct of 2022 General Election and promised better collaboration and partnership in the futur

title: DP Gachagua launches consultative forum for CCIOs to develop framework for engagement29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission led by the Chief Executive Officer Marjan H. Marjan participated in a three-day consultative forum that brought together the Executive and the Constitutional Commissions and Independent Offices (CCIOs), which was officially opened on 28th April 2024 by the Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, EGH. The forum developed a framework to guide the collaboration, coordination and engagement between the Executive and CCIOs besides creating a conclave for consultations and socialization. Further, the forum provided a platform through which CCIOs can contribute to the national development agenda and exchange views on the parameters of independence and interdependence in a public sector setting. The meeting also sought to identify and propose solutions to the challenges facing CCIOs in implementation of their mandate and sought to develop a legal mechanism of resolving the administrative issues between the Executive and CCIOs. The Deputy President underscored the role CCIOs play in helping the National Government fulfil its mandate and pledged that his office was ready to mediate on any issues between them to ensure that there is harmony in service delivery to the public. “I promise to support the CCIOs perform their duties without any hindrance,” said Gachagua. Speaking at the Forum, Judicial Service Commission (JSC) Chairperson, Chief Justice Martha Koome observed that the constitutional vision for our state institutions is one of a unified enterprise with each entity playing a distinct yet interconnected role in the broader schema of governance. The interactions between the Executive and the CCIOs should be characterized by a relationship of mutual support, including adequate resource allocation and restraint. However, she called for a clear oversight mechanism to ensure accountability of the Constitutional Commissions and Independent Offices. On his part, The Attorney General, Justin Muturi called for constructive engagement and collaboration among the CCIOs for them to effectively fulfill their Constitutional mandates. < Felix Koskei, the Head of Public Service, who officially closed the three-day forum, expressed his gratitude to the ODP for organizing the forum and urged the CCIOs to effectively conduct their oversight role as outlined in the Constitution. “The Executive is committed to collaborate and support the CCIOs to ensure your independence remains intact to guarantee efficient service delivery to the people of Kenya,” said Koskei. The forum discussed how CCIOs can positively contribute to Bottom-up Economic Transformative Agenda and other development agendas; best practices in performance management that can be adapted by CCIOs; key factors that can influence budget decisions and allocations for CCIOs such as government priorities, financial constraints and political considerations; best practices observed in terms of accountability and engagement between CCIOs and the Executive; the implications of interdependence and independence on decision making processes, resource allocation and overall effectiveness in driving development initiatives; strengthening the role and impact of CCIOs in realizing the constitutional vision of democratic governance and social justice with a focus on enhancing accountability, transparency and citizen-centers approaches among others. Executive No. 2 of 2023 on Organization of Government Mandate of the Office of the Deputy President (ODP), gave the ODP the liaison function with Constitutional Offices in matters that require intervention by the National Government including budgets, policy formulation and implementation of their recommendations.

title: IEBC meets donor partners, apprises and lauds their positive collaboration to deliver 2022 GE29th Jul 2024
text: The Commission led by the CEO Marjan H. Marjan, MBS hosted a consultative meeting with the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) Kenya Office of Democratic Governance, Peace and Security (DGPS) and their partners the International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES) and Electoral Law and Governance Institute for Africa (ELGIA). The meeting sought to understand the Commission’s funding priority areas as well as apprise the donor partners on the areas where they offered support pre, during and post the 2022 General Election. The Commission highlighted the successful collaboration with the development partners in the last election specifically in electoral legal reforms; voter registration and electoral operations; research, electoral boundaries and risk management; public outreach and communication among others. The Commission's Secretary/CEO expressed gratitude to development partners for their support and reiterated the need for continuous collaboration to enable the Commission meet its mandate.

title: Commission hosts consultative meeting with Heads of Missions Governance Group24th Apr 2024
text: The Commission on Friday, with the support of United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), hosted an engaged session with the Heads of Missions Governance Group to appraise them on the status of its mandate. Commission Secretary and CEO Marjan H Marjan took the envoys through the Commission electoral and boundaries delimitation operations and assured the Group that the Commission was on course to deliver on its mandates despite challenges of budget cuts and lack of Commissioners. “The Commission has made big stride and achieved a great deal thanks to the vibrant collaboration that we have with your missions and I’m here to give a progress report on our processes, which you supported and enabled us to meet our mandate,” said Marjan. “Many of you might be wondering that IEBC has no Commissioners and therefore what are we doing in office. Well, the Commission is always working and in my status update I focus on specific mandate that IEBC has to deliver including conduct of election, boundaries delimitation and referendum.” Marjan observed that the Commission has been lauded for its good work conducting the 2022 General Election and has been feted locally and abroad. This has seen the Commission invited as part of observer team to Ghana and Zambia General Elections. On the other hand, the Commission received eight teams who visited to benchmark on IEBC electoral processes. “We went to Zambia specifically because they enrolled many youths in their Register of Voters (RoV) despite the high apathy among this group. We benchmarked on Zambia so as to learn how they achieved this to enable us to implement it in Kenya,” said Marjan. The meeting reiterated the need to fast track the review of the legal framework, in which the CEO informed the meeting that the Commission has made its submission to the joint Senate and National Assembly Justice and Legal Affairs Committee (JLAC) on a raft of amendments that was presented to the National Dialogue Committee (NADCO). The Heads of Mission Governance Group observed that they were satisfied with the Commission’s consultative and progress. Caroline Vicini, the Swedish Ambassador and Heads of Mission Governance Group lauded the Commission for its good work. “For the work you did in 2022 General Election, we are happy that you delivered. However, the development partners must not sit back now and say that Kenya electoral democracy has developed fully and stop supporting IEBC to continue meeting its mandate. Let us continue supporting the Commission,” said Vicini. The Group, which also had European Union Representatives, Neil Wigan, the British High Commissioner Heads of Mission, Governance Group, Madelena Monoja Deputy Resident Representative – Programmes, UNDP pledged to continue supporting the Commission in its course to deepen democracy in Kenya.

title: Commission submits views on proposed IEBC (Amendment) Bill, 2024 to joint JLAC Committee of Senate and National Assembly24th Apr 2024
text: The Commission appeared before the joint Senate and National Assembly Justice and Legal Affairs Committee (JLAC) led by Chairpersons Hon. George Murugara and Senator Hillary Sigei to submit views on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2024 (National Assembly Bill No. 10 of 2024) at the County Hall, Mini Chambers, Nairobi. The Commission Secretary and CEO, Marjan H. Marjan, MBS led the IEBC team in the presentation of its Memorandum before the committee. Marjan appreciated the progressive nature of the bill in enhancing the efficacy of the Commission and its processes. The Bill intends to review provisions of Sections 2 (Interpretation); 7A (Vacancy in the office of Chairperson and members); 10 (Secretary to the Commission); 36 (Procedure for delimitation of electoral boundaries); First Schedule (Procedure for appointment of Chairperson and Members of the Commission), Second Schedule (Provisions of conduct of the business and affairs of the Commission) and Fifth Schedule (Provisions relating to boundary delimitation) of the IEBC Act considering emerging reforms. The IEBC made submissions which highlighted the relevant legal framework, justification, and proposals for review. In addition, IEBC submitted comments on the implications of the proposed amendments.

title: CEO Marjan speaks on opportunities, risks involved with AI use in elections management24th Apr 2024
text: Information Systems Audit and Control Association (ISACA) Kenya Chapter held its annual conference in Mombasa from 8th to 12th April 2024. The conference, which is themed Digital Trust: Charting the Course for a Resilient Future explored the ground-breaking confluence of digital trust, emerging technology, and the evolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Commission Secretary and CEO Marjan H. Marjan, MBS, who is a member of ISACA Kenya Chapter and one of the key speakers in the conference, made a presentation on the opportunities and inherent risks in the use of AI in elections management. “Election Management Bodies (EMBs) stand to benefit from the emergence of AI especially in voter education, elections results management and communication. AI tools can be used to quickly translate electoral and digital documents to difference languages, countercheck and verify election results as well as analyze and identify patterns in provisional voting among others,” said Marjan. The CEO added that the Commission deployed AI in the 2022 General Election by using a WhatsApp Bot to disseminate electoral information, analyzing the Register of Voters (RoV) to check for deduplications and partnered with International Foundation for Election Systems (IFES) to develop a hate speech digital and social media monitoring tool. “AI is being used to develop and spread misinformation, disinformation and mal-information on digital and social media platforms, escalate hate speech, increase the digital divide among other risk factors,” said Marjan.

title: Commission senior management trains on use of ArcGIS mapping software in election2nd Apr 2024
text: The Commission, supported by United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), held a training session for its senior management staff on the use of ArcGIS Mapping Software in delivering its mandate with technical backing from ESRI East African, which is a global leader in geospatial solutions. ESRI East Africa had earlier trained the technical officers on the new technology and assisted the Commission to develop and customize some of its applications in line with its activities. The Commission Secretary and CEO Marjan H. Marjan, who opened the two-day training session, said it was important to bring on board the senior management staff to get apprised on the technology, showcase the customized applications and demonstrate how it can be utilized to promote efficiency. “I thank the UNDP and ESRI for their support to enable the Commission build capacity on the new technology. This training will help us plan strategically in accordance with the law. It will also enable the Commission to build on its knowledge base,” said Marjan. “The managers here act as the gatekeepers and with this knowledge they will be able to work well with the officers to implement it. With that I ask all to be focused and gain as much knowledge as possible,” added Marjan. The ArcGIS mapping Software training can be used throughout the electoral cycle in implementing the activities and programmes the Commission undertakes in elections management and boundaries delimitation. “Once incorporated, the Commission will be able to use the software to monitor its election operations such as voter registration and polling day activities and respond to challenges in real time,” said Everton Namasake of ESRI Eastern Africa. The CS/CEO also had a meeting with Samuel Kimani, the ESRI Eastern Africa CEO and expressed the Commission’s desire to collaborate with the company to utilize its experience and knowledge in geospatial solutions.

title: Music Copyright Society of Kenya requests IEBC to oversee conduct of directors elections2nd Apr 2024
text: The Commission hosted a delegation from the Music Copyright Society of Kenya (MCSK) led by their CEO Dr. Ezekiel Mutua to strategize and plan on the conduct and management of the MCSK’s forthcoming Directors and member committees elections scheduled for 15th April 2024. The meeting resolved to draw an MoU that will guide the conduct and management of the elections to ensure fairness, transparency and credibility in the process. The delegation also paid a courtesy call to the Commission Secretary/CEO Mr. Marjan Hussein Marjan in his office. The imminent MCSK elections come on the backdrop of IEBC successfully conducting the LSK elections on 29th February 2024.

title: Johns Hopkins University students visit IEBC, study policies on good governance2nd Apr 2024
text: The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission(IEBC) last week hosted students from the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Affairs (SAIS) from Washington D.C. USA. The delegation comprising of graduate students are in the country for a study tour to learn about policies in different areas of good governance. The IEBC team, which was led by the Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan H. Marjan, MBS discussed how the Commission conforms to the principles of good governance while undertaking its mandate, and policies governing elections management in Kenya.

title: Commission reviews Strategic Plan, to inform development of 2027 Election Operation Plan2nd Apr 2024
text: The Commission, in collaboration with the International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES), held a two-day workshop from March 20-21 to evaluate the performance of the IEBC's Strategic Plan, 2020 – 2024 that expires in June. The evaluation report will be critical in the development of the Strategic Plan for the years 2024-2028, which will factor in the upcoming General Election in 2027. The assessment aims to align the Commission operations by incorporating recommendations from the Post Election Evaluation (PEE) Report that highlighted the lessons learnt, technological advancements, good governance practices, legal and regulatory requirements, as well as the Commission’s long-term vision. This will enable the Commission to improve its electoral operations and processes and ensure that it fulfils its mandate of conducting fair and transparent elections. Ruth Kulundu, Deputy Commission Secretary – Operations, speaking during the opening of the workshop, on behalf of the Commission Secretary/CEO Marjan H. Marjan, MBS underpinned the current strategic plan, which has been implemented as part of Vision 2030, Mid-Term Expenditure Framework Plans, and the Big Four Agenda. She emphasized on the need to assess the Strategic Plan and align the new one with the current realities. Currently, the government's economic policy is based on Vision 2030, Mid-Term Expenditure Framework Plans, and the Bottom-up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA), which necessitates a review and development of a new Strategic Plan to align it with the current realities. “As we prepare for the upcoming phase of planning for the 2024 – 2028 Strategic Plan, it is important to assess and plan the activities and decisions we carried out in the 2020-2024 Strategic Plan period,” said Kulundu. The DCS thanked IFES for their continued support and asked members of staff to make reference to past strategic plans and see what worked and what didn’t work in addition to engaging the staff through questionnaires to establish the most effective roadmap for the Commission. Obadiah Keitany, Deputy Commission Secretary- Support Servies expressed gratitude to IFES for their support and reiterated that initiating the strategic plan is of utmost importance as it will form the framework on which the new Elections Operations Plan (EOP) will be based. He also emphasized that one of the pillars the Commission should focus on in the 2024-2028 Strategic Plan should be refining the organizational culture. The workshop was led by Rushdi Nackerdien, Senior Global Advisor - Training & Capacity Building at IFES, who served as the lead facilitator. Dorothy Atieno, Senior Programs Officer at IFES, also played a key role. The workshop was attended by the senior management of the Commission, including directors as well as technical staff.

title: IEBC attends electoral management bodies conference, discusses use of AI in 2022 GE2nd Apr 2024
text: The Commission took part in the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Conference for Electoral Management Bodies (EMBs) in Africa that was organized by Yiaga Africa in Nairobi on 16 March 2024. The Commission Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Marjan Hussein Marjan, MBS, shared insightful perspectives on the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) by EMBs. In his presentation, Mr. Marjan emphasized the practical applications of AI that the Commission employed during the 2022 General Election including voter registration to avoid deduplication of voters, and use of mobile applications aimed at providing electoral related information with the aim of empowering voters to make informed decisions. The CEO underlined the important collaboration the Commission has forged with the International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES) that led to creating a social media monitoring tool powered by AI that monitored instances of hate speech. In addition, the Commission partnered with META to address misinformation and disinformation. Marjan's presentation underscored the need for capacity building and accountability of EMBs as they embrace AI in order to enhance efficiency.

title: IFES Director for Africa pays courtesy call, pledges continuous support to Commission2nd Apr 2024
text: International Foundation for Electoral Support (IFES) Regional Director for Africa Clara Cole last week paid a courtesy call to IEBC's Commission Secretary/CEO, Marjan Hussein Marjan, MBS. The two had fruitful discussion including evaluating IFES' support to IEBC over time and agree on potential areas for collaboration to assist the Commission meet its Constitutional mandate. The discussions also covered IEBC's approach to managing misinformation and disinformation, digital media and social media influence on elections management, pre-election activities, status of the electoral boundaries exercise and the National Dialogue Committee report. Additionally, the meeting deliberated on the proposed artificial intelligence guidelines for election management bodies that were unveiled during the Artificial Conference held in Nairobi on 16th and 17th March 2024. The CEO appreciated the immense support that IFES provided in the lead up and during the 2022 General Election and the renewed support that was availed post 2022 GE. Mr Marjan also shared a number of possible areas for partnership and collaboration between IEBC and IFES. Ms. Cole, on her part, acknowledged the Commission's appreciation and assured that IFES will continue to commit to the collaboration and will explore all the opportunities available to ensure the Commission delivers on its mandate. Ms. Cole was accompanied by Mr. Obaje Ukeh, Country Director IFES Kenya, Ms. MacKenzie Hempe, Senior Programs Officer IFES Africa and Ms. Dorothy Atieno, Senior Programs Officer IFES Kenya.

title: Faith Mony Odhiambo voted President as Commission conducts election for Law Society of Kenya2nd Apr 2024
text: The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) called upon the Commission to conduct its elections on February 29 across the country. Albert Gogo, the Nairobi County Elections Manager, was appointed the Returning Officer for the election, which were conducted in all the counties. LSK had declared vacant the position of President, Vice-President, Members of Council, Male Representative to the Judicial Service Commission (JSC) and Members of the Advocates Disciplinary Tribunal (ADT). Faith Mony Odhiambo was voted in as the new Law Society of Kenya president succeeding Eric Theuri, who served as President for a two-year term from March 2022. Odhiambo edged out four other candidates after she registered 3,113 votes ahead of her closest rival Peter Wanyama who secured 2,165 votes. Carolyne Kamende finished third in the tight race with 888 votes. Fourth placed Bernard Ng'etich managed 833 votes, while Njoki Mboce got 511 votes. Odhiambo led in all the 6 polling stations at the Milimani Law Courts, and regions like in Nyeri, Homa bay, Nanyuki, Kisii, Machakos, Kisumu and Nakuru. A total of 7,521 out of the 15,715 registered members cast their vote with only 11 votes being declared invalid.

title: Second batch of Lesothos electoral officials benchmark on election security management2nd Apr 2024
text: The Commission hosted the second delegation of officials from the Independent Electoral Commission of Lesotho as well as various security outfits, who are in the country to learn on election security management. The delegation was keen on learning how Kenya plans, trains and deploys its security personnel during elections. Deputy Commission Secretary (DCS) - Support Services, Mr. Obadiah Keitany led the IEBC Senior Management in welcoming and sharing insights, experiences and lessons learnt from the management of the 2022 General Election. He noted that the Commission was glad to share its experiences as well as learn from its peers so as to continually improve electoral processes in Kenya. “We are humbled by your decision to benchmark with us on how to conduct and manage election. This endorsement is a clear show of the trust you have with our processes,” said Keitany. Dr. Meshack Lomoywara, Ag. Director Research, Electoral Boundaries and Risk Management (DREB&RM) took the delegation through the Election Security Arrangement Programme (ESAP), which is a strategic collaboration between the Commission and security agencies in the country. “Kenya has adopted a mixed model that brings together security agencies and the Commission to ensure effective coordination of electoral security,” said Dr. Lomoywara. “Since 2013 the Commission has collaborated with National Police Service (NPS) to ensure structured provision of election security Implementation predicated on lessons from 2007 Post-election violence and the imperatives of Article 81 of the Constitution- Free and fair elections are elections that are free from violence, intimidation, improper influence and corruption.” Linus Onyango, the Risk and Electoral Security Officer, gave a breakdown on how ESAP is structured and its Coordination mechanisms. “At the top is a High-level Election Security Policy Forum co-chaired by IEBC Chairperson and Inspector General of Police (IGP), followed by ESAP Policy advisory forum co-chaired by IEBC Vice-chairperson and Deputy IGP, a Multi – Agency Technical Coordination Committee is next. An Election Security Hub at IEBC is at the bottom and is responsible for to coordinating ESAP activities at the Constituencies, Counties and finally at the National Tallying centre. The Hub has linkages with women situation room and other early warning systems in the country,” said Onyango. IEC Operations Inspector and head of delegation Mr. Kotsoane Motsie expressed his gratitude for the hospitality and time the Commission took to share the experiences, lessons learnt and challenges in managing election saying it will go a long way in informing their own operations back at home. “Thank you very much IEBC for your warm welcome and hospitality, we have learned a lot in the two days we were here in your office. We are impressed with the way IEBC manages elections and we shall take what we have learned home to help us improve our processes,” said Motsie. Ruth Kulundu, DCS – Operations say Kenya still has a lot to do to continuously improve its processes in election management and the collaboration and partnership with other election management bodies will help them attain this objective. “We have come along way as a Commission and there is more, we need learn so that we may always improve our processes. We hope for continued mutually beneficial relationship between the two EMBs,” said Kulundu.

title: IEBC presents Budget Policy Statement to parliaments Justice Legal Affairs Committee2nd Apr 2024
text: The Commission appeared before the National Assembly’s Departmental Committee on Justice and Legal Affairs (JLAC) to consider the 2024 Budget Policy Statement (BPS). Led by Commission Secretary/Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Mr Marjan Hussein Marjan, MBS, the Commission reported to JLAC that it presented a Kshs. 19 billion budget to the National Treasury for recurrent and development expenditure but was allocated Kshs 4.35 billion. The Commission’s development requirement that was present for consideration to the National Treasury was Kshs 1.276 billion, but it was allocated a paltry Kshs77 million in the financial year 2023/24 to complete ongoing projects and settlement of development pending bills. Moreover, the commission was allocated Kshs24.32 in the 2024-25 financial year to implement three projects being construction of office block and warehouse in Nyandarua, Busia and Turkana counties. With the current allocation, the Commission is unable to fully undertake its planned activities including conduct of boundaries delimitation exercise, settle pending bills and construct Uchaguzi Centre. Marjan noted that the Commission has successfully concluded the Geo-data collection in all the 47 counties and documented administrative units for each of the gazette sub-location to ensure current boundaries reflect the true status on the ground. However, there is a continuous gazettement of the sub-locations by the Executive and the delays in carrying out the delimitation exercise may force the Commission to factor in new units when the exercise commences. Indeed, lack of Commissioners has delayed the planned data validation and consolidation and the budget allocated to caary out the exercise has not been allocated. “We continue to wait the reconstitution of the Commission and further guidance on the remaining activities in the boundaries delimitation, which include conduct of public hearings across the country. These activities can only be made possible through adequate funding,” said Marjan. The CEO in addition, said the Commission was affected negatively through Supplementary Estimates 1 budget cuts. The cut by Parliament on the boundary delimitation to nil/zero allocation made the Commission suffer a budget reduction of Kshs. 53.8 million which had been incurred and spent on preparation for boundaries delimitation exercise. The CEO requested the Committee to consider and allocate the funds to cater for the expenditure already incurred. The JLAC Chairperson, Hon. George Murugara, pledged to present the Commission’s report and requests to the National Assembly’s Budget and Appropriations Committee for consideration.

title: Electoral Commission of Lesotho tours IEBC headquarters on benchmarking mission2nd Apr 2024
text: The Commission is hosting the delegation from Independent Electoral Commission of Lesotho, who are in the country to learn on various electoral matters so as to improve their own processes. The team from Lesotho which is on a three-day study tour are keen on learning about register development, maintenance and management; general elections and referenda; results transmission and publication; use of Artificial Intelligence in the electoral process; and deployment of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in elections. Commission Secretary and CEO Mr Marjan Hussein Marjan, MBS welcomed the Lesotho delegation noting that the Commission does not take for granted their visit, which serves as a confidence vote in the electoral process in Kenya. “I welcome you to Kenya. You have stated in your request that you want to learn about issues to do with election operation, management and referendum. We have a good team here to guide you and I hope our experience and what we share here will help you to improve your election management,” said Marjan. Also present was Deputy Commission Secretaries for Operation Ruth Kulundu and Support Services Obadiah Keitany. The Independent Electoral Commission of Lesotho was led by its Chief Executive Officer Mpaiphele Maqutu, who lauded the IEBC for great job conducting the 2022 General Election, which offers hope to other Election Management Bodies (EMBs) as they endeavor to attain similar standards. “We have come to Kenya to learn from your experience on the successes you have recorded in conduct of your election. We would like to know the technologies you used and how we can learn from it,” said Maqutu. The four-member Lesotho delegation had Maqutu (team leader), Motloi Sekoala, Silas Tsoeu the IECL Systems Administrator and Phenethe Mapepe, the IECL Senior Database Administrator. Michael Ouma, the Commission’s Director of Information, Communication and Technology who is the chairperson of the delegation, reiterated that Kenya’s election is conducted manually and not electronic.

title: Commission retreats to Machakos to review Election Campaign Financing regulations2nd Apr 2024
text: The Commission, with support from Transparency International Kenya, is holding a workshop in Machakos county to review the Election Campaign Financing regulations. Campaign financing, which is a key focus area in the electoral legal reform agenda, is responsible for setting contribution and spending limits pursuant to Section 5(b) of the Elections Campaign Financing Act, 2013. In the 2017 and 2022 General Elections, the Commission set contributions and spending limits, but were not approved by the National Assembly and thus not implemented. Following the 2022 revocation, Katiba Institute filed a case challenging Parliament's resolution and certain provisions of the Act. While delivering its ruling in the matter, the Court directed the Commission to develop Regulations, subject them to public participation and put in place structures to set Contribution and Spending Limits pursuant to Section 5(b) of the Elections Campaign Financing Act, 2013. Mr. Obadiah Keitany, the Deputy Commission Secretary in charge of Support Services, underscored the significance of collaborative endeavors in shaping the democratic landscape. The Court in its judgment directed the Commission to proactively and timeously come up with the Regulations contemplated under Article 88(4)(i) of the Constitution so that this country has in place the requisite Regulations and the necessary spending limits. In doing so, the Commission will be promoting constitutionalism. “The Commission appreciates the tireless and committed engagement of Transparency International- Kenyan Chapter on the issue of implementing the Elections Campaign Financing Act, 2013,” said Keitany. The DCS lauded the Directorate of Legal Services for the vital role it plays in the enactment of electoral laws and regulation, which have enabled the Commission to deliver on its Constitutional mandate.

title: IEBC hosts Malawi Electoral Commission and discusses election technology, EDR processes2nd Apr 2024
text: The Commission, last week played host to a delegation from Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC), which toured Kenya to learn more on electoral dispute resolution mechanisms and use of technology in elections. The 17-member delegation representing MEC, Malawi Judiciary and UNDP was led by the Malawi’s Justice of Appeal Ophrah Dorothy and was welcomed and hosted by the Commission Chief Executive Officer Marjan Hussein Marjan. “This is a mutual learning experience, IEBC and MEC will greatly benefit from this visit,” Marjan said. Dorothy said Malawi delegation will use the knowledge gained to develop a comprehensive Electoral Dispute Resolution (EDR) Framework to effectively manage electoral disputes and also procure electoral technology solutions to improve the efficacy of their electoral processes. Malawi’s intends to strengthen its ICT and cyber security in electoral processes and the Commission visited Kenya to benchmark on its successful deployment of technology in conduct of elections, especially in carrying out voter registration, voter identification and results transmission. “The tour provides invaluable insights that will inform review on Electoral Dispute Resolution (EDR) Framework, Rules of Procedure for the Malawi Judiciary, and the overall management of electoral matters,” observed Justice Dr. Chifundo Kachale, Chairman MEC. “Electoral disputes are bound to happen, we are here to learn from our peers IEBC on how they dealt with electoral disputes before and after the 2022GE as we prepare for the Malawi 2025GE scheduled for 16th September,” said Andrew Mpesi, the Chief Elections Officer MEC. Isaack Otieno, the UNDP Malawi Chief Technical Advisor - Elections, retaliated UNDP’s commitment to support EMBs in the conduct and management of elections as part of its #DeepeningDemocracy project. During their second day in Nairobi, the team was taken through the Management of Elections in Kenya with an overview of the 2022 General Election and toured the Commission’s premises. Director Legal Services, Chrispine Owiye, gave the history of the EDR in Kenya, briefly highlighting its implementation in 2013, 2017 and 2022 General Elections. “Article 88(4) (e) of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010 confers on the IEBC the mandate to settle electoral disputes, including disputes relating to or arising from nominations, but excluding election petitions and disputes after the declaration of election results,” said Owiye. Mr Owiye added, “In tandem with Article 88 (4) (e), Section 74 of the Elections Act, 2011 and Section 4 of the IEBC Act, 2011 further reinforces the Commission’s mandate on dispute resolution and requiring the determination of disputes within ten (10) days of lodging complaints.” “Election dispute resolution plays a critical role in the pre-election period. It provides a good platform for scrutiny of pre-election processes. It also ensures compliance with values and principles in the Constitution to protect political rights and enhance electoral justice,” said Ruth Makuthu, the Ag. Manager Legal Reforms Political Parties Liaison and Campaign Financing. The team was told that the Commission heard and determined 324 disputes from registration of candidates and further heard and determined 6 party disputes pre #2022GE. As part of IEBC’s commitment to moving Kenya towards a stronger democracy, the Commission allowed all complaints to be filed free of charge, and it heard and determined all disputes within 10 days. “In keeping with the prescriptions of Chapter Six of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010 on leadership and integrity, the Commission is obligated to ensure that only persons who meet the educational, moral and ethical requirements are registered and cleared to contest as candidates in election,” observed Senior Legal Officer, Nancy Koros. Later, the delegation met with Political Parties Disputes Tribunal (PPDT) and International Commission of Jurists (ICJ). This was besides visiting the Commission’s Election Technology Warehouse, the National Warehouse and The Bomas of Kenya facility that is used as the National Tallying Centre during the General Elections. At the Election Technology Warehouse, IEBC officers took the Malawi delegation through the Kenya Integrated Election Management System (KIEMS), Candidates Registration Management System (CRMS) and Results Transmission System (RTS).
