title: DCI Arrests Prime Suspect in Joy Kanini Murder
text: DCI Arrests Prime Suspect in Joy Kanini Murder By: PHIDEL KIZITO | 12th Jul 2026 | 3 min read Listen Suspect in murder of Joy Kanini Gathu,John Nderitu Mureithi/courtesy NAIROBI, Kenya, Jul 12 – Detectives from the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) have arrested the prime suspect in the murder of 25-year-old Joy Kanini Gathu, ending a month-long investigation into the killing that shocked the country after her dismembered body was found dumped in Nyeri County. The DCI said John Nderitu Mureithi was arrested on the night of July 10 along the Nanyuki–Isiolo Road in Timau, Meru County, as he allegedly attempted to flee to Uganda. Detectives recovered four mobile phones during the arrest, including one believed to belong to the deceased, which investigators say will form a key exhibit in the case. “The suspect, John Nderitu Mureithi, was arrested on the night of July 10, 2026, along the Nanyuki–Isiolo Road while allegedly attempting to flee to Uganda.” “A search conducted immediately after his arrest led to the recovery of four mobile phones, among them the deceased’s handset, which has been secured as a key exhibit in the ongoing investigation.” You might also like INTERPOL Taskforce meets in Nairobi to strengthen Africa’s fight against child sexual abuse Suspected Drug Mules Nabbed With 13.9kg of Cannabis at Highway Roadblock Infant Reunited With Mother After Eight-Day Search According to investigators, the suspect and the victim were involved in a confrontation inside the suspect’s house in Ngangarithi Estate, Nyeri, on June 9 that allegedly turned fatal. Detectives say investigations indicate the suspect later dismembered the body and disposed of the remains in different locations in an alleged attempt to conceal the crime and frustrate investigations. The arrest follows significant forensic and digital breakthroughs in the case. Investigators had earlier established that the victim’s missing SIM card had been inserted into another mobile phone after her disappearance, providing crucial digital evidence that linked the suspect to the investigation. Police also found the suspect in possession of Joy’s mobile phone, despite his earlier claim that she had removed the SIM card before disappearing. Joy, the daughter of a pastor from Lamuria in Laikipia County, was last seen after meeting her parents in Nyeri before informing them she would not travel home because of work commitments. Two days later, the suspect reportedly contacted her family claiming she had gone missing and accompanied them to report the matter to police. Detectives later identified inconsistencies in his account as the investigation progressed. Her dismembered body was discovered stuffed inside a sack in Ngangarithi Estate on June 11, with investigators using distinctive birthmarks to confirm her identity after DNA testing had initially been considered. At the time, some body parts, including the head, had not been recovered. The suspect is expected to appear before court on Monday, July 13, where detectives will seek custodial orders to allow them to complete investigations. title: UN experts say M23's 'reign of terror' in DRC must end
text: UN experts say M23's 'reign of terror' in DRC must end By AFP July 22, 2026 01:21 (EAT) Add as a Preferred Source on Google Follow us Follow on Whatsapp Follow on Google Follow on Twitter Members of the M23 rebel group ride on a pickup truck as they leave their position for patrols amid conflict between them and the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC), in Goma, eastern DRC, January 29, 2025. REUTERS Audio By Vocalize United Nations experts appealed on Tuesday for an end to the "reign of terror" imposed by the M23 armed group in DR Congo, citing civilian reports of sexual torture and murder. Since its resurgence in 2021, the M23 group has taken control of vast tracts of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, which has major reserves of gold, tin and coltan, and has been plagued for three decades by conflict involving a plethora of countries and armed groups. "Rapes, gang rapes, violent assaults and killings of civilians are a common feature of M23's modus operandi," the experts said. "While these crimes are not exclusive to M23, the number of individuals affected is staggering and must end." They noted that UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres had reported more than 90,000 cases of sexual violence related to armed conflict there in 2025. M23, they said, had "established a de-facto system of authority in territories under its control in which arbitrary arrest and detention, torture (including sexual torture), forced labour and forced armed recruitment are being used to exercise control over the civilian population". Locals had also reported "abductions, arson and blackmail", the experts said. People arbitrarily arrested were being jailed in overcrowded and unsanitary "unofficial" prisons, where they were systematically deprived of food, water and medical care, the experts continued. Inmates recounted "repeated physical violence including daily beatings" and said several had died in custody. In many cases, detainees were only released if their relatives paid, said the experts. They called for a thorough investigation of the "unacceptable" violence, insisting that all parties to the conflict should respect international law and protect civilians. They called for a resurrection of the moribund US-mediated ceasefire signed in December 2025 between the Rwandan-backed M23 and the DRC government. The deal includes a provision for US industries to gain privileged access to the eastern DRC's vast mineral wealth. title: Africa CDC says US should lift Ebola travel restrictions on Uganda
text: Africa CDC says US should lift Ebola travel restrictions on Uganda By AFP July 22, 2026 12:39 (EAT) Add as a Preferred Source on Google Follow us Follow on Whatsapp Follow on Google Follow on Twitter A member of the Doctors Without Border (MSF) personnel at the Elikya clinic Ebola treatment center in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, on June 5, 2026. (Photo by GLODY MURHABAZI / AFP) Audio By Vocalize Africa's top public health agency said Tuesday it does not support travel bans in response to the continent's worsening Ebola outbreak, urging the United States to lift restrictions imposed on Uganda. The appeal comes days after Washington tightened travel restrictions linked to the current Ebola outbreak, which originated in the Democratic Republic of Congo, on travellers from the DRC, Uganda and South Sudan. Speaking at an African Union health summit in the Ghanaian capital, Accra, Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention director-general Jean Kaseya said the agency was "not advising" travel bans. Public health experts have argued during previous Ebola outbreaks that travel bans hinder medical supplies and personnel and disrupt trade, instead pushing for disease surveillance and case isolation. Kaseya said he had written to US health secretary Robert F. Kennedy requesting the lifting of travel restrictions on Uganda specifically, arguing the country had gone three weeks without recording a new Ebola case and discharged its last patient on July 16. "There is no reason for the US to continue with this travel restriction," he said, adding that countries should not be "punished" for being transparent about disease outbreaks. Even as he opposed travel restrictions, Kaseya warned the outbreak itself was escalating rapidly. "If we don't stop this outbreak today, it will be the worst one that the world will be documenting," he said. There have been 2,344 confirmed cases of Ebola in the DRC, including 930 deaths, since the outbreak was declared in mid-May, according to the World Health Organization. Uganda has reported 20 cases and two deaths -- mostly Congolese citizens who crossed the border. The Africa CDC estimates it needs $1.4 billion to contain the outbreak, almost three times the $518 million initially projected last month. "If we don't have this money, we will not stop this outbreak," Kaseya said, adding African countries had so far pledged about $110 million. He said health authorities should be monitoring nearly 97,000 contacts linked to confirmed Ebola cases but were currently following only about 8,500 people. The remarks came as ministers from across Africa met during the African Union summit, where leaders are expected to adopt a roadmap on Wednesday aimed at strengthening health systems, improving epidemic preparedness and accelerating progress towards ending AIDS by 2030. trending now CCTV shows Constable Kimani as cell sentry on night of Ojwang murder 13 hours ago Three more suspects linked to Chaiiwali café robbery arrested 15 hours ago CCTV footage shows Albert Ojwang alive moments before being locked in police cells New UK PM Burnham stamps authority with cabinet shakeup 17 hours ago Pauline Njoroge resigns from Jubilee Party to join Linda Mwananchi 13 hours ago latest stories Tags Africa CDC DRC Uganda Ebola Have a story? title: 'All or nothing!' Karua says will not settle for deputy president post, to support United Opposition candidate
text: 'All or nothing!' Karua says will not settle for deputy president post, to support United Opposition candidate By Joseph Muia July 21, 2026 11:20 (EAT) Add as a Preferred Source on Google Follow us Follow on Whatsapp Follow on Google Follow on Twitter A screengrab of PLP leader Martha Karua speaking on Citizen TV's The Explainer Show on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. Audio By Vocalize People's Liberation Party (PLP) leader Martha Karua has ruled out taking up the position of deputy president under a United Opposition arrangement, maintaining she will either vie for the presidency or support whoever is selected as the coalition's flag bearer. Speaking on Citizen TV's The Explainer on Tuesday night, Karua said she would respect the coalition's agreed selection process and back the candidate chosen, provided the process is conducted according to the rules set by the alliance. Karua, who was picked as late Raila Odinga's running mate in the last election under the Azimio Coalition umbrella, expressed satisfaction that she was content with the opportunity to deputise Raila and would not wish to deputise any other candidate in the opposition faction. "I will support the one who is chosen in accordance with the rules we have set. The only thing I will not do is be a running mate. That one I say. I've no wish to be a running mate. I did a good run with Raila Odinga. That's just about enough. But it's all or nothing," she said. Karua maintained that her decision was final, and that if another opposition leader emerged as the preferred candidate, she would fully support them but would not accept the deputy president slot. "If I am not the flag bearer, I will support hundred per cent. But I won't be a running mate," she added. Asked what her priorities would be in the first 100 days if elected president, Karua said restoring the rule of law would be her immediate focus to ensure the interests of citizens are protected, and lawbreakers face justice. "I will immediately enforce the rule of law; make sure that we adhere to the rules of the game that we have made as Kenya, safeguard Kenyans' interests first, ensure that quality services are delivered in the critical areas of health, education, and service delivery in the various areas," she said. Karua expressed confidence that a functioning government could be restored within 90 days, citing her experience during the NARC administration that took office in 2002. "Within 90 days, you should have a functional state. And I say that with boldness because I saw it when we came in as the NARC administration. No law was changed, not even the constitution. And within a matter of days, things were running differently," she said. According to the PLP leader, effective leadership begins with those at the top setting the right example, arguing that public servants and citizens respond positively when leaders match their actions with their promises. "When the top shows that their actions match their words, the people of Kenya take cue. Government employees take cue. And Kenyans are very good at assisting leadership in doing the work that is supposed to be done," she said. Karua consequently underscored that restoring normal public service delivery and holding lawbreakers accountable, regardless of their status, would form the foundation of her administration. "So I would ensure that services, normal service delivery, resume, and that lawbreakers, whatever their position or rank, are dealt with. And that's how you begin transformation," she said. title: New bill proposes digital protest notices, tighter rules on police conduct during demonstrations
text: New bill proposes digital protest notices, tighter rules on police conduct during demonstrations By Stephen Letoo July 21, 2026 09:14 (EAT) Add as a Preferred Source on Google Follow us Follow on Whatsapp Follow on Google Follow on Twitter Police take position behind a temporary barricade erected outside parliament buildings in anticipation of anti-government protests to commemorate the struggle against government oppression on annual day of protest known as Saba-saba in Nairobi on July 07, 2026. TONY KARUMBA / AFP Photo by TONY KARUMBA / AFP Audio By Vocalize The Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR) and the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) have developed a legislative proposal to facilitate peaceful demonstrations. Under the proposed Bill, notices to picket or present public petitions can now be submitted through email, WhatsApp messages or even by affixing the notices near police stations. The bill comes after the High Court sitting in Kisumu delivered a landmark judgment directing the government to develop and publish clear legal and operational regulations governing public assemblies, demonstrations, picketing and the use of force by law enforcement officers. The Bill, which is now awaiting public input, states in part that "an organiser of an assembly, picket or demonstration shall notify the regulating officer of the intention to hold the assembly, picket or demonstration." According to the proposals, the notification shall be in writing and may be delivered in person to the regulating officer or to the regulating officer's electronic address. Where it is not possible to deliver the notification in person or to the electronic address of the regulating officer, the notice may be affixed to the official premises of the regulating officer or in a public place near or around the official premises of the regulating officer. Where protests are spontaneous and occur without prior notice, regulating officers are required to protect participants, journalists, healthcare workers, observers and monitors, as well as public and private property. According to the new proposals, a regulating officer may prohibit the conduct or holding of an assembly, picket or demonstration where there is a credible, specific and imminent risk of death, serious violence, serious injury or extensive destruction of property. Where plain-clothed police officers are deployed in relation to a demonstration, they shall be deployed for the purposes of gathering criminal intelligence and monitoring suspected offenders who have infiltrated or intend to infiltrate the assembly, picket or demonstration. According to the Bill, a firearm may be used to disperse an assembly, picket or demonstration only where it is strictly necessary to protect life or prevent serious injury, and in accordance with the Constitution and the National Police Service Act. title: Repatriated Kenyans seek gov't support to rebuild lives after South Africa return
text: Repatriated Kenyans seek gov't support to rebuild lives after South Africa return By Melita Ole Tenges July 21, 2026 08:50 (EAT) Add as a Preferred Source on Google Follow us Follow on Whatsapp Follow on Google Follow on Twitter A file image showing a group of Kenyans repatriated from South Africa outside the State Department for Diaspora Affairs. Audio By Vocalize Kenyans repatriated from South Africa earlier this month following xenophobic violence are appealing to the government for financial support to rebuild their lives after returning home. The representatives of the 477 Kenyans evacuated from South Africa gathered at the State Department for Diaspora Affairs, saying they are facing severe financial hardship after returning home jobless and without a source of income. They want the government to provide financial assistance to enable them to restart their businesses and rebuild their lives. "The key agenda is on funding to help us get back on our feet. We are not here against our government; we are actually here thanking our government for the good work,” said Baylian Wambugu, leader of the returnees. Ali Jele Sambul, a returnee, added: "Muhimu ni tunataka leo tupate habari nzuri, tupewe pesa tuanze biashara. Leo siondoki hapa, afadhali nifungwe na serikali." Beyond financial struggles, the returnees say many of their children, who were born in South Africa, lack Kenyan birth certificates, making it difficult to enrol them in local schools. Others returned without identification documents, while some families are still seeking government assistance to repatriate the bodies of relatives who died in South Africa. "All the children who were born in South Africa don't have birth certificates. Very many others came from prison without IDs. We also have cases of some of the deaths that happened—we want those bodies brought back,” Wambugu said. "There is no way you can bring a child from elsewhere and expect them to continue with school immediately. You need documentation that will indicate the way forward,” Ruth Wambui, another returnee, added. The returnees have also appealed to the Kenyan government to engage South African authorities over five-year entry bans they say were imposed on them upon their departure, arguing that the restrictions should be lifted once the security situation stabilises. "When we arrived at South African immigration, all of us, despite having official letters, were issued with a five-year ban from returning to South Africa. We want the Kenyan government to engage South Africa so that the ban can be lifted,” stated Julius Mwangi, another returnee. trending now CCTV shows Constable Kimani as cell sentry on night of Ojwang murder 13 hours ago Three more suspects linked to Chaiiwali café robbery arrested 15 hours ago CCTV footage shows Albert Ojwang alive moments before being locked in police cells New UK PM Burnham stamps authority with cabinet shakeup 17 hours ago Pauline Njoroge resigns from Jubilee Party to join Linda Mwananchi 13 hours ago latest stories Tags Citizen Digital South Africa violence xenophobia Have a story? title: Autopsy confirms hotel intern who fell from Upper Hill building died from multiple fractures
text: Autopsy confirms hotel intern who fell from Upper Hill building died from multiple fractures By Gatete Njoroge July 21, 2026 08:39 (EAT) Add as a Preferred Source on Google Follow us Follow on Whatsapp Follow on Google Follow on Twitter Audio By Vocalize Margaret Wambui, the 21-year-old woman who died after falling from the rooftop of Altura Apartments in Upper Hill, succumbed to multiple severe fractures, an autopsy has confirmed. The post-mortem examination conducted at the Nairobi Funeral Home established that Wambui died on the spot following the fatal fall. Sources familiar with the investigations have told Citizen TV that Wambui spent more than 40 minutes on the rooftop of the 34-storey building taking photographs before the incident. Detectives who have reviewed CCTV footage from the building have ruled out any third-party involvement in her death. Three days after learning of their daughter's death, Wambui's family and friends gathered at the Nairobi Funeral Home for the post-mortem examination, which was conducted in the presence of a family-appointed pathologist. The findings confirmed the family's worst fears. "We had our family doctor present during the post-mortem, and we have been informed that she indeed died from the fall. Almost every part of her body was fractured, although her head did not sustain any injuries," said Maina Gathogo, a relative. With the autopsy now complete, the family says it is hoping detectives investigating the mysterious death will establish what transpired on the rooftop on Saturday night. The sudden death has left the family devastated, with Wambui's dream of building a career in the hospitality industry cut short. "Our prayer is that detectives from the DCI Kilimani continue with the investigations so they can establish what happened. If she jumped, we want to know what could have driven her to make such a decision," Gathogo said. Sources close to the investigation who have reviewed CCTV footage from Altura Apartments told Citizen TV that Wambui entered the premises shortly after 8 p.m. She was later captured on the rooftop, where she spent more than 40 minutes taking photographs while a security guard patrolled the area. Investigators say that at one point she was seen standing at the edge of the rooftop. It is believed that shortly before the fall, the security guard on duty had briefly left the area to use the washroom. That was reportedly the last time Wambui was seen alive. "There is CCTV footage showing what transpired, and as a family we would like to be allowed to see it so that we can find closure and be satisfied with the findings," Gathogo said.
